Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Will who loved exploring new places. One day he went on a hike with his mom. As they were walking, they saw a big pile of lumber on the ground.

"Mommy, what is that?" asked Will.

"It's a pile of lumber," she explained. 

Will wanted to examine the pile of lumber more closely. He walked around it, looking at it carefully. Suddenly, he felt something soft. This made Will very curious. He leaned in closer and saw a little mouse.

The mouse was very miserable. He had been stuck between two pieces of lumber for days, and was too weak to escape. 

Will quickly grabbed his mom and said, "Mommy, we have to help the little mouse!" 

His mom smiled and said, "Of course we can help the mouse. Let's see if we can move the lumber to set him free."

Together, they worked to carefully move the lumber and eventually, the mouse was free. Will smiled as the little mouse hopped away. 

"That was a great adventure today," said Will.

His mom smiled and replied, "Yes, it was! We have to remember to always help others in need!"

Lily smiled back and hugged her dad. She felt better and happier. She said, "Thank you, dad. You are the best. I love you."

They decorated the cake with frosting and sprinkles and candles. They waited for mom to come home and sang happy birthday to her. Mom was surprised and delighted. She loved the cake and the kitchen and Lily and dad. She said, "You are the best family ever. I love you."

They ate the cake and laughed and hugged. They had a wonderful day. Lily was happy. She was a famous chef and a brave girl. She had the best family ever. She loved them.

"But mom, I like it. It is my insect. I caught it. Please, can I keep it?" Lily begged.

But Anna refused. She shook her head and pushed her bowl away. She said, "No, no, no. I do not like radishes. I only like carrots and potatoes and noodles."

Lily says, "No, I want the black block. It is mine. I found it first." She holds the block tightly. Ben says, "But I like the black block. It is the best block. It is shiny and smooth. Please, let me have it." He tries to pull the block from Lily.

They both tug on the block. They do not want to share. They start to cry. Their mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting over the block. She says, "What are you doing? Why are you crying?"

Lily and Ben tell their mom that they both want the black block. They both request the block. Their mom says, "There is only one black block. You cannot both have it. You have to take turns or find another block. How many black blocks do you have?"

Lily and Ben look at their blocks. They see that they have zero black blocks. They only have one black block. They feel silly. They say, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Ben." They hug each other. They decide to share the black block. They use it for their tower and their train. They are happy. Their mom is happy too. She says, "Good job, Lily and Ben. You are very kind and smart." She gives them a kiss. They smile. They keep playing with the blocks. They have fun. The end.

Sara liked to look at the magazine with her mom. The magazine had many pictures of people who did fun things, like singing, dancing, or acting. Sara wanted to be like them when she grew up. She admired them a lot.

One day, Sara saw a picture of a girl who looked like her. She had the same brown hair, brown eyes, and freckles. The girl was smiling and holding a microphone. The magazine said she was famous and had a new song. Sara was very excited. She pointed at the picture and said to her mom, "Look, mom, she is like me! Can I be famous too?"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "You can be anything you want, Sara. You have a beautiful voice and a big heart. Maybe one day, you will be in a magazine too."

Sara was happy. She dreamed of singing on a big stage, with many people clapping and cheering for her. She asked her mom, "Can we listen to her song, mom? Please?"

Her mom nodded and turned on the radio. She said, "Sure, Sara. Let's listen to her song. Maybe you can learn it and sing it with me."

Sara listened carefully to the song. She liked it very much. It was catchy and fun. She tried to sing along, but some of the words were hard for her. She asked her mom, "What does this word mean, mom? And this one?"

Her mom explained the words to her. She said, "This word means you are happy and proud of yourself. And this one means you don't care what others think of you. You just do what you love."

Sara nodded. She understood. She said, "I like these words, mom. They are good words. I want to be happy and proud and do what I love."

Her mom said, "You are already happy and proud and doing what you love, Sara. You are singing with me. And I love you very much."

Sara smiled and hugged her mom. She said, "I love you too, mom. You are the best. And you are famous to me."

Sara loves to watch princess movies. She has a pink dress and a crown that she wears when she watches. She likes to pretend that she is a princess too.

One day, Sara wants to watch her favorite princess movie with her brother Tom. But Tom does not like princess movies. He likes to watch cars and robots. He says princess movies are boring and silly.

Sara is upset. She does not want to watch cars and robots. She wants to watch her princess movie. She says to Tom, "Please, Tom, can we watch my movie? It is very fun and pretty. You will like it too."

But Tom says, "No, Sara, we cannot watch your movie. It is very long and dumb. I want to watch my movie. It is very cool and exciting. You will like it too."

Sara and Tom start to argue. They both want to watch their own movie. They do not want to share the TV. They do not listen to each other. They make a lot of noise.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the living room. She sees Sara and Tom fighting. She is not happy. She says to Sara and Tom, "Stop, Sara and Tom, stop! You are being very rude and selfish. You need to learn to take turns and respect each other's choices. If you cannot do that, you will not watch any movie at all."

Sara and Tom are quiet. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They do not want to make Mom angry. They do not want to lose their TV time. They say to Mom, "We are sorry, Mom. We will be nice and share. We will watch both movies. We will take turns and watch what the other one likes."

Mom smiles. She is glad that Sara and Tom are sorry and willing to compromise. She says to Sara and Tom, "That is very good, Sara and Tom. I am proud of you. You are being very kind and fair. You can watch both movies. But first, you need to hug and say sorry to each other."

Sara and Tom hug and say sorry to each other. They are not upset anymore. They are happy. They watch both movies. They enjoy both movies. They learn something new from each movie. They have fun together. They are good siblings.

Lily was a fairy who liked to help people. She had a magic wand that could restore things that were broken or lost. One day, she saw a boy crying in the park. He had a toy car that was missing a wheel.

Lily flew over to the boy and said, "Don't cry, I can help you. I can restore your toy car with my magic wand. Watch this!" She waved her wand and said a spell. The toy car sparkled and a new wheel appeared.

The boy was very happy and thanked Lily. He hugged his toy car and played with it. Lily smiled and flew away to find someone else to help.

But Lily did not know that her spell had a side effect. The boy's toy car was not only restored, but also alive. It could talk and move by itself. It was very confused and curious about the world. It wanted to explore and have fun.

The boy was surprised and scared when his toy car started to talk and drive away. He tried to catch it, but it was too fast. He shouted, "Stop, come back, you are my toy car!"

The toy car did not listen. It said, "I am not your toy car, I am a car. I want to see the world. Bye bye!" It zoomed out of the park and into the street, causing chaos and confusion. People and cars were honking and yelling at it.

Lily heard the noise and saw the trouble. She realized that she had made a mistake. She flew after the toy car and said, "Stop, stop, you are not a car, you are a toy car. You belong to the boy. You are making a mess. Let me fix you."

The toy car did not want to be fixed. It said, "No, no, I like being a car. I don't want to be a toy car. Go away!" It tried to escape from Lily, but she was faster. She caught up with it and waved her wand again. She said another spell. The toy car stopped and lost its sparkle. It became a normal toy car again.

Lily took the toy car and flew back to the park. She found the boy and gave him his toy car. She said, "I'm sorry, I made a bad spell. Your toy car is not alive anymore. It is just a toy car. Please forgive me."

The boy was relieved and happy. He said, "It's okay, I forgive you. Thank you for restoring my toy car. It was scary when it was alive. I like it better when it is just a toy car. You are a good fairy."

Lily smiled and said, "You are welcome. I'm glad you are happy. I learned a lesson. I have to be careful with my spells. Goodbye!" She flew away and hoped that she would not make any more mistakes.

Anna and Ben wonder what olives are. They open a jar and take out some olives. They taste them. They are salty and sour. Anna and Ben make another face. They do not like olives either.

Anna and Ben are scared. They run to their room. They do not want Mama to strike them. They do not understand why Mama likes olives. They think olives are yucky. They wish they never climbed the tree. They are not curious anymore.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the garden. They saw a big lime tree with many green fruits. They wanted to pick some limes to make juice.

"Look, Tim, there is a big lime up there. Can you get it for me?" Kim asked.

"OK, Kim, I will try. But the lime is very high and hard to reach. I need a stick." Tim said.

Tim found a long stick and tried to poke the lime. He pushed and pushed, but the lime did not fall. He pushed harder and harder, but the lime did not move.

"Tim, be careful. The stick might break." Kim warned.

"I can do it, Kim. I just need to push a little more." Tim said.

But as he pushed, the stick snapped in half. The broken end flew into the air and hit Tim in the eye. Tim screamed and dropped the stick. He covered his eye with his hand and felt a lot of pain.

"Tim, Tim, are you OK? What happened?" Kim asked.

"Ow, ow, ow. The stick hit me in the eye. It hurts so much. I can't see." Tim cried.

Kim ran to Tim and hugged him. She was very scared and sorry. She did not know what to do.

"Tim, I'm so sorry. I should not have asked you to get the lime. It was too hard and dangerous. We should have asked Mom or Dad for help." Kim said.

But it was too late. Tim had lost his eye. He had to go to the hospital and wear a patch. He could not play in the garden anymore. He was very sad and angry.

The moral of the story is: Do not try to do things that are too hard or risky for you. Ask for help from someone who knows better. Be careful with sharp or heavy things. They can hurt you or others.

"What is that?" Anna asked.

"It is soup. It is good for you. Try some," Mom said.

Anna and Ben did not want to try the soup. They were frightened. They thought the soup was yucky. They made faces. They said, "No, thank you."

Mom was sad. She said, "Please, eat your dinner. It is not yucky. It is tasty. I made it with love."

Anna and Ben looked at Mom. They saw that she was sad. They did not want to make Mom sad. They loved Mom. They decided to be brave. They took their spoons. They scooped some soup. But Lily did not see a rock on the grass. She stumbled and fell down. She hurt her knee and started to cry. Ben stopped and ran to her. He said, "Are you okay, Lily? I'm sorry you fell down."

Ben said, "I want juice, please." Mommy said, "Okay, Ben. Here you go." She poured him some juice and gave him a glass. She said, "Drink your juice and be careful. Don't spill it. And don't touch the wine. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig holes and make mud pies. They had a lot of fun with their toys and their dog, Spot.

But then, Lily saw something shiny in the dirt. She picked it up and rubbed it with her hand. It was a coin, with a face and some letters on it.

"Look, Ben, look what I found!" Lily said, holding the coin up.

Ben came over and looked at the coin. He shrugged. He did not think it was very interesting.

"It's just a coin, Lily. It's old and dirty. There are many coins like that," he said.

Lily frowned. She thought the coin was special. She wondered who had it before and what they used it for. She wanted to keep it and show it to Mom and Dad.

"No, Ben, it's not just a coin. It's a treasure! Maybe it belonged to a pirate or a king or a fairy. Maybe it has magic powers. Maybe it can make wishes come true," she said.

Ben rolled his eyes. He did not believe in pirates or kings or fairies or magic. He liked to play with cars and trucks and robots. He thought Lily was silly.

"Come on, Lily, let's go play something else. Coins are boring. Let's go chase Spot or swing on the tire or build a fort," he said.

Lily shook her head. She did not want to play something else. She wanted to keep the coin and find out more about it. She put it in her pocket and smiled.

"OK, Ben, you go play something else. I'll play with my treasure. Maybe I'll find more. Maybe I'll be rich and famous and happy," she said.

Ben shrugged again. He did not care about Lily's treasure. He ran off to play with Spot and his toys. He had a lively time.

Lily stayed in the yard. She dug more holes and looked for more coins. She did not find any, but she did not mind. She had her treasure and her imagination. She had a lovely time.

One day, a boy named Ben saw a cop on the street. He was wearing a blue shirt and a hat with a star. He had a big belt with many things on it. Ben was curious and wanted to talk to the cop.

He ran to the cop and said, "Hello, mister. What are you doing?"

The cop smiled and said, "Hello, little one. I am a cop. I help people and keep them safe. Do you want to see my badge?"

Ben nodded and the cop showed him his badge. It was shiny and had a number on it. Ben liked it and asked, "Can I hold it?"

The cop said, "Sure, you can hold it. But be careful, it is important. It shows that I am a cop and I have a job to do."

Ben took the badge and held it in his hand. He felt proud and happy. He said, "Wow, this is cool. I want to be a cop when I grow up."

The cop said, "That's great. Being a cop is a good job. You can help people and make a difference. But you have to work hard and learn a lot. And you have to be brave and kind."

Ben said, "I can do that. I like to help people and be brave and kind. And I like to learn new things. Can you teach me something?"

The cop said, "Of course. I can teach you something. Do you know what this is?" He pointed to a whistle on his belt.

Ben said, "No, what is it?"

The cop said, "This is a whistle. I use it to make a loud noise when I need to get someone's attention. Do you want to try it?"

Ben said, "Yes, please."

The cop gave him the whistle and said, "Blow on it gently, like this." He showed him how to blow on the whistle.

Ben followed his example and blew on the whistle. It made a loud noise that made everyone look at them. Ben laughed and said, "That's fun. Can I do it again?"

The cop said, "Sure, you can do it again. But only once more. Then you have to give it back to me. It is not a toy. It is a tool. I need it for my job."

Ben said, "OK, I understand." He blew on the whistle one more time and then gave it back to the cop. He said, "Thank you, mister. You are very nice. And you have a very cool job."

The cop said, "You are very welcome, little one. You are very polite. And you have a very bright future. Remember, you can be anything you want to be. Just follow your dreams and work hard. And always be brave and kind."

Ben said, "I will, mister. I will. Goodbye, mister."

The cop said, "Goodbye, little one. Have a good day."

Ben waved to the cop and ran back to his mom. He told her what he learned from the cop. He said, "Mom, I met a cop today. He was very nice. He let me hold his badge and blow his whistle. He taught me about his job and how to be brave and kind. He said I can be a cop when I grow up. Can I, mom?"

His mom hugged him and said, "Of course, you can, my son. You can be anything you want to be. You are a smart and good boy. I am proud of you. And I love you."

Ben hugged her back and said, "I love you too, mom. And I love the cop. He was different from other people. He was a hero."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of curiosity, respect, gratitude, and aspiration. It shows that different people have different jobs and roles in society, and that we can learn from them and appreciate them. It also shows that we can pursue our dreams and goals, as long as we work hard and have good values.

One day, Anna and Ben went to play in the snow. They put on their coats, hats, boots and mittens. Anna had red mittens and Ben had blue mittens. They made a snowman, threw snowballs and slid down a hill.

"Look, Anna, I found a yellow mitten in the snow!" Ben said. He picked it up and showed it to Anna.

"That's not your mitten, Ben. That's someone else's mitten. You have blue mittens, remember?" Anna said.

"I know, but maybe I can match it with another yellow mitten. Then I will have two pairs of mittens!" Ben said. He liked the yellow mitten. It was bright and soft.

Anna shook her head. "That's not a good idea, Ben. That's a careless thing to do. What if the person who lost the yellow mitten is looking for it? They will be sad and cold. You should put it back where you found it." She said.

Ben thought for a moment. He did not want to make anyone sad or cold. He realized that Anna was right. He was being careless. He said sorry to Anna and put the yellow mitten back in the snow. He hoped that the person who lost it would find it soon.

"Good job, Ben. You are a kind and honest boy. Come on, let's go home. It's getting dark and cold. We can have some hot chocolate and cookies." Anna said. She took Ben's hand and they walked back to their house. They were happy and warm. They still had their own mittens. They matched.

One day, a little fairy named Lily was flying in the forest. She liked to look at the flowers and the birds and the sun. She was happy and sang a song.

But then she heard a loud noise. It was a roar. It came from a big cave. Lily was scared. She flew closer to see what it was.

Inside the cave, she saw a big lion. He was lying on the ground. He looked sad. He roared again.

"Hello, Mr. Lion," Lily said. "Why are you sad?"

The lion looked at Lily. He was surprised. He did not see many fairies in the forest.

"Hello, little fairy," he said. "I am sad because I hurt my paw. I stepped on a thorn and it is very sore. I cannot run or play or hunt. I am hungry and lonely."

Lily felt sorry for the lion. She flew closer and looked at his paw. She saw the thorn. It was small but sharp.

"Maybe I can help you," she said. "I have some magic dust. It can make things better. Can I try?"

The lion nodded. He trusted Lily. She was kind and brave.

Lily sprinkled some magic dust on the lion's paw. She said a magic word. The thorn came out. The paw healed. The lion felt no pain.

"Thank you, little fairy," he said. "You are very nice. You made me happy. Can you be my friend?"

Lily smiled. She was happy too. She made a new friend.

"Yes, Mr. Lion," she said. "I can be your friend. We can play and sing and have fun. But first, can you teach me how to roar?"

The lion laughed. He liked Lily. He taught her how to roar. They roared together. They sounded like music. The forest was filled with joy.

You will only get cauliflower for breakfast, lunch and dinner. You will only get cauliflower for every meal. You will only get cauliflower for the rest of your life. Is that what you want?"

Sara thinks for a moment. She says, "Yes, yes, yes. I want cauliflower for the rest of my life. I love cauliflower. Cauliflower is the best. Cauliflower, cauliflower, cauliflower!"

Sara's mom shakes her head. She says, "Okay, Sara. You can have cauliflower for the rest of your life. But don't come crying to me when you get tired of it and want something else. You made your choice. You have to live with it. Good luck with your cauliflower."

Sara smiles. She says, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I am happy with my cauliflower. Cauliflower, cauliflower, cauliflower!" She hugs her spoon and her little piece of cauliflower. She does not know what she is missing. She does not care. She only cares about cauliflower. She stays with cauliflower. She is the cauliflower girl.

"Where are we going, Sara?" Tom asked.

"We are going to the park, Tom. We will see the ducks and the swings and the slide," Sara said.

"Uh-oh, Sara. The dog is angry. What do we do?" Tom said.

Sara was not afraid of the dog. She knew the dog was just playing. She stopped the wagon and smiled at the dog.

"Hi, dog. Do you want to be our friend? You can come with us to the park," Sara said.

The dog wagged its tail and licked Sara's face. Sara giggled and petted the dog.

"See, Tom. The dog is not angry. He is nice. He just wanted to say hello," Sara said.

Tom was still scared of the dog. He thought the dog was big and loud and mean. He did not want to pet the dog. He hid behind Sara.

"No, Sara. The dog is bad. He wants to bite us. Let's go away," Tom said.

Sara shook her head. She thought Tom was ignorant. He did not know anything about dogs. She wanted to teach Tom that dogs were fun and friendly.

"Tom, you are silly. The dog is good. He will not bite us. He will play with us. Come on, Tom. Don't be ignorant. Be brave," Sara said.

She took Tom's hand and pulled him out of the wagon. She gave him a dog biscuit and showed him how to feed the dog. The dog took the biscuit gently and wagged its tail again.

Sara smiled and hugged Tom. She was happy that Tom learned something new. She was proud of herself for being a good driver and a good teacher.

Lila and Ben were playing in the yard. They saw a fat fox hiding behind a bush. The fox had a big tail and small eyes. Lila and Ben wanted to pet the fox.

"Come here, fox," Lila said. "We are nice. We want to be your friends."

But the fox was scared. He did not like people. He ran away from Lila and Ben. He tried to squeeze through a hole in the fence. But he was too fat. He got stuck in the hole.

"Help, help," the fox cried. "I am stuck. I cannot move."

Lila and Ben heard the fox. They ran to the fence. They saw the fox's head and tail on both sides of the hole.

"Are you okay, fox?" Ben asked. "Do you need help?"

"Yes, please," the fox said. "Can you pull me out?"

Lila and Ben nodded. They grabbed the fox's tail and pulled. The fox felt a lot of pain. He yelped and whimpered.

"Ow, ow, ow," the fox said. "You are hurting me. Stop pulling."

"Sorry, fox," Lila said. "But you are too fat. You need to lose some weight."

The fox felt ashamed. He knew he ate too much. He wished he was thinner.

"Maybe you can push me from the other side," the fox said.

"Okay," Ben said. He ran to the other side of the fence. He pushed the fox's head. The fox felt more pain. He groaned and moaned.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch," the fox said. "You are hurting me. Stop pushing."

"Sorry, fox," Ben said. "But you are too fat. You need to exercise more."

The fox felt angry. He did not like being pushed and pulled. He wished he was free.

"Maybe you can dig a bigger hole," the fox said.

"Okay," Lila said. She ran to get a shovel. She dug a bigger hole in the fence. The fox felt some relief. He wiggled and wriggled.

"Ah, ah, ah," the fox said. "You are helping me. Keep digging."

"Okay, fox," Lila said. She dug and dug. She made the hole big enough for the fox to squeeze through. The fox felt happy. He thanked Lila and Ben.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you," the fox said. "You are kind. You are my friends."

"You are welcome, fox," Lila and Ben said. "We are glad you are okay."

The fox smiled. He waved his tail. He ran away from Lila and Ben. He decided to eat less and run more. He wanted to be healthy and fit. He wanted to see Lila and Ben again.

The end.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The mom making a cake for dessert and setting the timer is a setup for the payoff of the cake being burned and the twins not getting any dessert.

They wrestled, rolled on the ground and growled loudly. Suddenly, the bear felt a sharp pain in his paw! He quickly ran away, scared and yelping in pain.

The bear ran home, his paw hurt badly. He knew he had been too eager to fight and he learned to be more careful next time!

He waved the little girl over and spoke to her softly. He told her that the station was a very special place and he had lots of stories to share!

The little girl stayed and listened to the old man's stories and then she went back to the train station. The train was leaving, but she had learned something very important. She knew that the station was a special place and that she could learn new things when she paid attention and listened to everyone.

The penguin was so happy and trustingly followed the polar bear. They soon came across a warm and cozy cave. The penguin looked up at the polar bear and said, "Will this be my new home?" The polar bear nodded and said kindly, "Yes, little penguin. You can trust me to look after you here."

The penguin smiled and said a thankful goodbye to the polar bear. He snuggled into the cave and fell asleep, feeling safe and secure knowing he had something to trust.

Once there was a house in the woods. Standing at the window was a little girl. She watched the world go slow by. From the corner of her eye, she saw a deer. Slowly it stepped closer and closer. Then, suddenly a gentle gust of wind passed by and the girl heard it again; a soft whisper. The deer had a message for the little girl. The deer told her to enjoy the view, no matter how slow the world goes by.

The girl smiled to herself and whispered back a thank you to the deer. Then, slowly, the deer stepped away and continued on its journey.

So, he asked the zookeeper for help, and the zookeeper showed him how to wrap the present. The monkey was happy and excited to give the present to his friend. From that day on, he learned that it's okay to ask for help and that being friendly is important.

Suddenly, someone shouted, "Hey! That's my square!" It was a mom who had been walking by. She was really mad that Jack had taken her square. She started to yell at him.

Jack was scared and he started to cry. "I'm sorry," he said. 

The mom felt bad. She stopped yelling and gave Jack a big hug. "It's ok," she said. "Just don't touch things that belong to other people." 

Jack was happy and he promised never to take anything that wasn't his again. He ran off to play with his friends. He was so glad that the mom didn't yell at him anymore.

"No, let's make a bridge," Sam says. He takes some pieces of track away. "Then the train can go up and down."

Tim and Sam start to argue. They pull and push the pieces of track. They make a mess.

"Stop it!" Tim says. "You are ruining my loop!"

"Stop it!" Sam says. "You are ruining my bridge!"

They are not happy. They are not having fun.

Then, they hear a noise. It is Mom. She comes into the room. She sees the mess. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"

Tim and Sam look at Mom. They look at the mess. They feel bad.

"We are sorry, Mom," Tim says.

"We are sorry, Mom," Sam says.

Mom sighs. She helps them clean up the mess. She gives them a hug.

"Next time, you need to decide together," Mom says. "Playing with trains is easy and fun, but only if you share and cooperate."

Tim and Sam nod. They say sorry to each other. They decide to make a new track. They make a loop and a bridge. They let the train go round and round, and up and down. They smile and laugh. They are friends again.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play with dolls. They had many dolls of different sizes and colors. They also had a big house for their dolls, with rooms and furniture and clothes. They were very happy when they played with their dolls.

One day, Tom had a new idea. He said to Lily, "Let's display our dolls. We can put them on the table and show them to everyone. They are so pretty and nice. Maybe someone will give us a prize for having the best dolls."

Lily agreed. She thought it was a fun idea. They took their dolls and their house and put them on the table in the living room. They arranged them neatly and carefully. They smiled and waited for someone to see their display.

But no one came. Tom and Lily were sad and bored. They wondered why no one cared about their display. They decided to go and look for someone to show their dolls to.

They left the table and went to the kitchen. There they saw Tom's big brother, Ben. Ben was eating a sandwich. He saw Tom and Lily and said, "What are you doing here? Go away. You are annoying."

Tom and Lily said, "We want to show you our display. We have many dolls and a house. They are very pretty and nice. Come and see."

Ben rolled his eyes. He said, "I don't care about your display. Your dolls are stupid and boring. They are not real. They are just toys. You are too old to play with dolls. You should play with something else."

Tom and Lily felt hurt and angry. They said, "No, our dolls are not stupid and boring. They are real to us. We love them. You are mean and rude. You don't know anything about dolls."

Ben laughed. He said, "Fine, I'll show you how much I know about dolls. Follow me."

He took his sandwich and went to the living room. Tom and Lily followed him, hoping he would change his mind and like their display. But they were wrong.

Ben reached the table and saw the dolls and the house. He said, "Wow, what a disgusting display. It makes me sick. Look at these ugly dolls. They have no eyes, no nose, no mouth. They have no hair, no arms, no legs. They have no clothes, no shoes, no hats. They are not dolls. They are trash."

He threw his sandwich at the display. The sandwich hit the dolls and the house. It made a big mess. The dolls and the house were covered with bread and cheese and ham and lettuce and tomato and mayonnaise. They looked dirty and smelly and ruined.

Tom and Lily screamed. They ran to the table and tried to save their dolls and their house. They cried and shouted, "Stop it, stop it, stop it. You are bad, you are bad, you are bad. You ruined our display. You ruined our dolls. You ruined our play. We hate you, we hate you, we hate you."

But Ben did not stop. He laughed and laughed. He said, "This is fun. This is the best display ever. I love it. I love it. I love it."

He grabbed more sandwiches and threw them at the display. He made more mess. He made more noise. He made more trouble.

Tom and Lily were very sad. They could not stop him. They could not fix their display. They could not play with their dolls. They lost their friends. They lost their happiness. They had a bad ending.

"Look at our castle, Sam! It is the best castle ever!" Tom said.

"Yes, it is, Tom! We are the best builders ever!" Sam said.

But then, they saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was black and furry and had a terrible bark. The dog saw the castle and wanted to play with it. The dog jumped on the castle and knocked it down. The dog dug in the sand and buried the tower, the wall and the door. The dog wagged its tail and barked happily.

Tom and Sam were very sad and angry. They cried and shouted at the dog.

"Go away, dog! You are a bad dog! You ruined our castle!" Tom said.

"Leave us alone, dog! You are a mean dog! You destroyed our work!" Sam said.

But the dog did not understand. The dog thought they were playing with him. The dog licked their faces and tried to be friendly.

A lady came and saw what happened. She was the dog's owner. She apologized to Tom and Sam and called the dog.

"I'm so sorry, boys. He is a good dog, but he doesn't know any better. He likes to play with sand and thinks everything is a toy. Come here, Rex!" she said.

She put a leash on the dog and walked away. She smiled and waved at Tom and Sam.

Tom and Sam stopped crying and looked at each other. They realized that the dog did not mean to hurt them. He was just curious and playful. They felt sorry for being rude to him.

"Maybe we were too harsh, Tom. The dog was not bad, he was just silly." Sam said.

"You're right, Sam. The dog was not mean, he was just happy." Tom said.

They decided to forgive the dog and make a new castle. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but they can always start over. They also learned that animals have feelings too, and they should be kind to them. They had fun and made new friends.

Mama sighed and hugged Lila. "I know, sweetie, but you have to be patient. The vest is for warmer days, not for snow. You can still be a star in your coat, you know. You just have to believe in yourself."

Lila looked at Mama and frowned. She didn't like the coat. It was big and heavy and itchy. She wanted to feel the sun on her skin and the wind in her hair. She wanted to be free and happy.

"Mama, please, can I wear my vest? Just for a little bit? Please, please, please?" Lila begged.

Mama shook her head. "No, Lila, you can't. It's too cold, you'll get sick. And we have to go now, we're late for school. Come on, let's go."

Lila pouted and stomped her feet. She didn't want to go to school. She wanted to stay home and play with her vest. She wanted to be a star.

But Mama took her hand and led her to the car. She buckled her seat belt and gave her a kiss. "I love you, Lila. You're my star, no matter what you wear. Maybe tomorrow it will be warmer and you can wear your vest. But today, you have to be patient and brave and smart. Can you do that for me?"

Lila nodded slowly. She still wanted her vest, but she loved Mama too. She wanted to make her happy. She wanted to be a good girl. She looked out the window and saw a snowflake. It was white and shiny and beautiful. It made her smile.

Maybe Mama was right. Maybe she could still be a star in her coat. She just had to believe in herself.

"Look, Lily, the moon is so bright!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, it is very pretty. Do you think it can talk?" Lily asked.

Tom laughed. "No, silly, the moon can't talk. It is just a big rock in the sky."

But then they heard a soft voice coming from the moon. It said, "Hello, Tom and Lily. I can talk to you. I am the moon."

Tom and Lily were very surprised. They looked at each other and then at the moon.

"Hello, moon. How can you talk to us?" Tom asked.

"I can talk to you because I am magic. I can see you and hear you. I like to watch you play and learn. You are very smart and kind." The moon said.

"Wow, thank you, moon. You are very nice and beautiful. We like to watch you too. You make the night glow." Lily said.

The moon smiled. "You are welcome, Lily. I am happy to be your friend. Now it is time for you to go to bed. I will watch over you and keep you safe. Good night, Tom and Lily."

"Good night, moon. Thank you for talking to us. We love you." Tom and Lily said.

They waved to the moon and ran inside to tell their mom and dad about their new friend. They dreamed of the moon and the stars all night.

Sara and Tom were scared and ran to the bench. They grabbed their dolls and held them tight. They felt guilty and sad. They did not mean to make a mess and hurt the park. They said, "We are sorry, mister. We did not know. We just wanted to play."

The man saw their faces and softened a bit. He said, "Well, now you know. Waste is not for playing. It is for throwing away in the trash can. Next time, play with your dolls or something else that is not waste. And don't forget to say sorry to the park, too."

One day, they bring a ball to the shore. They throw it to each other and catch it. Sometimes the ball falls in the water and they run to get it. They laugh and shout.

"Tom, catch!" Anna says and throws the ball high in the air.

Tom jumps and tries to catch it, but he misses. The ball flies over his head and lands far away in the water.

"Oh no!" Tom says. "The ball is gone!"

They run to the water and look for the ball. But they can't see it. The water is too deep and too blue.

"Where is the ball?" Anna asks.

"I don't know," Tom says. "Maybe a fish took it."

They are sad. They like the ball. They don't want to lose it.

They sit on the sand and watch the water. They hope the ball will come back.

But the ball does not come back. The sun goes down and the sky turns pink and purple. It is time to go home.

"Come on, Tom and Anna," their mom says. "It's getting dark. We have to go."

They get up and follow their mom. They forget to take their bucket and shovel. They leave them on the dry sand.

They walk to the car and get in. They are still sad about the ball.

"Maybe we will find it tomorrow," Tom says.

"Maybe," Anna says.

They look out the window and see the shore. They see their bucket and shovel. They remember them.

"Mom, we forgot our bucket and shovel!" they say.

"Oops!" their mom says. "We'll get them tomorrow. Don't worry."

They nod and smile. They are not so sad anymore. They still have their bucket and shovel. They can play with them tomorrow. And maybe they will find their ball too.

Lila and Tom are brother and sister. They like to play in their room. They have a lamp that makes light. The lamp is old and poor. It has a crack on its shade and a loose wire.

One day, Lila and Tom hear a loud noise. It is a storm. The wind blows hard and the rain falls fast. They are scared. They run to their bed and hug each other.

"Tom, I don't like the storm. It is too loud and dark," Lila says.

"Me too, Lila. But we are safe here. We have each other and the lamp," Tom says.

He turns on the lamp. It makes a soft light. It makes them feel better.

But then, the storm gets worse. The thunder booms and the lightning flashes. The power goes out. The lamp stops working. It is dark again.

"Tom, the lamp is broken. What do we do?" Lila cries.

Tom thinks fast. He remembers that the lamp has a loose wire. He grabs the wire and twists it. He hopes it will work.

He says, "Lila, don't worry. I will protect you and the lamp. I will try to fix it."

He touches the wire to the lamp. It sparks. The lamp makes light again. Lila and Tom smile.

"Tom, you did it. You fixed the lamp. You are so brave and smart," Lila says.

"Thank you, Lila. You are so kind and sweet. We are a good team. We love each other and the lamp," Tom says.

They hug the lamp. They hug each other. They wait for the storm to end. They are not scared anymore. They are happy.

"Okay, let's open them. But first, we have to sing happy birthday and blow the candles," Anna says. She picks up a knife and cuts the cake. She gives Ben a big slice. She takes one for herself. They sit on the chairs and smile.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the pool. They had a big pool in their backyard, with blue water and toys. They wore swimsuits and goggles and jumped in the water. They liked to swim and splash and laugh.

One day, they saw something new in the pool. It was a big, green curtain that covered one side of the pool. They did not know what it was or why it was there. They were confused. They swam closer to the curtain and touched it. It felt soft and wet.

"Hello, is anyone there?" Tom asked, poking his head behind the curtain. He saw a man with a long beard and a hat. The man was holding a hose and spraying water on the pool wall. He looked surprised to see Tom.

"Who are you?" the man asked.

"I'm Tom, and this is Lily. We live here. Who are you?" Tom said, pointing to his sister.

"I'm Bob, the pool cleaner. I'm here to clean your pool. I put this curtain up to keep the dirt out of the water. Sorry, I didn't know you were here." Bob said.

"Oh, I see. Can we help you?" Lily asked, joining Tom behind the curtain.

"No, thank you. You can keep playing, but be careful not to touch the hose. It's very strong. And don't go under the curtain. It's not safe." Bob said.

"OK, thank you. Bye, Bob." Tom and Lily said.

They swam back to the other side of the pool and continued to play. They were not confused anymore. They learned something new. They liked Bob, the pool cleaner. He was nice. They hoped to see him again.

But there is nothing inside the box. It is dark and empty. Anna laughs and says "joke!"

Anna sees Ben's face. She feels sorry. She did not want to make Ben sad. She says "I'm sorry, Ben. I thought you would laugh. It was a bad joke. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily and Max are playing in the park with their dog, Spot. Spot is a big, black dog who likes to run and jump and bark. Lily and Max love Spot very much.

One day, they see something shiny in the grass. They run over to see what it is. It is a bone! A big, white bone with some meat on it. Spot sees the bone too and runs faster than Lily and Max. He grabs the bone in his mouth and runs away.

"Spot, come back!" Lily shouts. "That is not your bone!"

"Maybe it is a dinosaur bone!" Max says. "We should examine it!"

They chase after Spot, who is very happy with his bone. He finds a shady spot under a tree and starts to chew on it. Lily and Max catch up with him and sit down next to him.

"Spot, can we see your bone?" Max asks. "We want to examine it. Maybe it is very old and special."

Spot looks at Max and Lily with his big, brown eyes. He likes them, but he likes his bone more. He growls softly and holds the bone tighter.

"Please, Spot," Lily says. "We will not take your bone. We just want to look at it. Maybe we can share it."

Spot thinks for a moment. He likes to share, but he also likes to chew. He decides to make a deal. He lets go of the bone and pushes it towards Lily and Max. He wags his tail and barks.

"Thank you, Spot!" Lily and Max say. They pick up the bone and examine it. They see that it is not a dinosaur bone, but a cow bone. They see some letters on it. It says "BEEF".

"Look, Spot, this is a beef bone!" Max says. "It is from a cow. Do you like cows?"

Spot nods and licks his lips. He likes cows very much. He likes beef bones too.

Lily and Max smile and give the bone back to Spot. They pat his head and hug him. They say, "You are a good dog, Spot. We love you."

Spot wags his tail and barks. He loves them too. He chews on his bone and shares it with Lily and Max. They have a fun time in the park. They are happy.

Sam was a little boy who liked to learn new things. He liked to learn how to draw, how to sing, and how to play with his toys. But he did not like to learn how to eat his meal. He did not like the green things, or the red things, or the brown things on his plate. He only liked the yellow things, like cheese and bananas.

One day, his mom said, "Sam, you have to eat your meal. It is good for you. It will make you strong and healthy. And you can have a treat after you finish."

But Sam said, "No, I don't want to eat my meal. I only want cheese and bananas. And I want my treat now."

His mom said, "Sorry, Sam, but that is not how it works. You have to eat your meal first, then you can have your treat. And you have to try different things, or you will miss out on many yummy foods."

Sam was angry. He pushed his plate away and ran to his room. He slammed the door and sat on his bed. He did not want to talk to his mom. He did not want to eat his meal. He only wanted cheese and bananas. And his treat.

But after a while, he started to feel lonely. He did not hear his mom's voice, or his dad's voice, or his sister's voice. He did not hear the TV, or the radio, or the phone. He only heard his own tummy, making noises. He realized he was hungry. And he realized he was sad.

He got up and opened the door. He walked to the kitchen, where he saw his mom. She was sitting at the table, with a plate of food in front of her. She looked up and smiled.

"Hi, Sam," she said. "Are you ready to eat your meal?"

Sam nodded. He felt sorry for being rude. He said, "Yes, mom, I am ready. I am sorry for being mean. Can I try some of your food?"

His mom said, "Of course, Sam. You can try some of my food. And I have some cheese and bananas for you, too. And a treat."

Sam smiled. He sat down and took a bite of his mom's food. It was green, and red, and brown. But it was also tasty, and crunchy, and warm. He liked it. He said, "Mmm, this is good. What is it?"

His mom said, "It is salad, and chicken, and rice. Do you like it?"

Sam said, "Yes, I like it. Can I have some more?"

His mom said, "Sure, Sam. You can have some more. And I am proud of you for trying something new. You are learning how to eat your meal."

Sam felt happy. He ate his meal, and his cheese and bananas, and his treat. He hugged his mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

His mom said, "I love you, too, Sam. And I am glad you are not lonely anymore."

Lily was a good girl, but sometimes she did bad things. One day, she took a cookie from the jar when Mom was not looking. She ate the cookie and felt happy. But then, Mom saw the crumbs on Lily's face and asked her, "Did you take a cookie without asking?"

Lily felt scared and said, "No, Mom, I did not." But Mom knew she was lying. She said, "Lily, you should not lie to me. That is very bad. You are punished. You cannot watch TV or play with your toys for one hour. Go to your room now."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to be punished. She wanted to watch TV and play with her toys. She ran to her room and slammed the door. She cried and said, "I hate Mom. She is mean. I want a cookie."

But after a while, Lily felt sorry. She knew she did wrong. She knew Mom loved her and wanted her to be good. She wiped her tears and said, "I am sorry, Mom. I will not lie again. Can I come out of my room?"

Mom heard Lily and came to her room. She hugged her and said, "I forgive you, Lily. I love you. You can come out of your room. But you cannot have a cookie. You have to wait for dinner. You will be hungry if you eat too many cookies."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, Mom. I understand. I will wait for dinner. What are we having?"

Mom smiled and said, "We are having chicken and rice and carrots. And for dessert, we have a surprise. Do you want to know what it is?"

Lily's eyes lit up and said, "Yes, Mom. What is it?"

Mom said, "It is a cake. A special cake. It is for your birthday. Today is your birthday, Lily. You are four years old now. Happy birthday, my sweet girl."

Lily gasped and said, "Wow, Mom. Thank you. I love you. I love cake. Can I have a big piece?"

Mom said, "Yes, you can. But first, we have to go to the doctor. He will check you and give you a shot. It will hurt a little, but it will make you healthy and strong. Are you brave, Lily?"

Lily felt nervous and said, "I don't like the doctor. I don't like shots. They are scary."

Mom said, "I know, Lily. But they are important. And I will be with you. I will hold your hand and sing to you. And after the shot, you will get a sticker and a lollipop. And then we will go home and have cake. How does that sound?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "OK, Mom. I will go to the doctor. I will be brave. But can I have two stickers and two lollipops?"

Mom laughed and said, "Sure, Lily. You can have two stickers and two lollipops. You are a good girl, Lily. And a big girl. I am proud of you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best mom ever. Can we go now?"

Mom said, "Yes, Lily. Let's go. And don't forget to say goodbye to Dad. He will meet us at home later. He has a present for you, too."

Lily ran to Dad and hugged him and said, "Bye, Dad. I love you. See you soon."

Dad kissed her and said, "Bye, Lily. I love you, too. Have fun at the doctor. And happy birthday, my little princess."

Lily waved and said, "Thank you, Dad. You are the best dad ever. I can't wait to see your present."

Mom and Lily left the house and got in the car. They drove to the doctor. Lily was a little scared, but she was also excited. She knew she would have a great birthday. She had a loving family, a yummy cake, and a surprise present. She was a happy girl.

One day, they want to play with Bluey outside. They ask their mom if they can. Mom says yes, but they have to be careful. She gives them a bucket of water and a towel. Ben and Lily take Bluey and the bucket to the yard. They find a spot with grass and dirt.

"Hey, dog, stop! That is our sail!" Ben says.

"Give us back Bluey!" Lily says.

"Mom, the dog took our sail! The dog took Bluey!" Ben and Lily say.

They started to argue. They both wanted to be the boss. They did not listen to each other. They were ignorant.

Then they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a big dog. It was their neighbor's dog. It had escaped from its yard. It was angry and hungry. It saw Tom and Lily and ran towards them.

Tom and Lily were scared. They forgot about their sword and crown. They forgot about being the king and the queen. They ran to the house and shouted for help.

Their mom and dad came out. They saw the dog and called the neighbor. The neighbor came and took the dog away. He said he was sorry and that the dog was not mean, just playful.

Tom and Lily hugged their mom and dad. They were glad they were safe. They said they were sorry for being ignorant. They said they would share their sword and crown and be nice to each other.

They learned a lesson. They learned that being a knight or a princess or a king or a queen was not as important as being a friend. They learned that being ignorant was not good. They learned that being smart and kind was better.

Anna and Ben were twins who lived in a big house with their mom and dad. They had many toys and books and clothes. They were wealthy, but they did not know it. They thought everyone had the same things as them.

One day, they went to the park with their mom. They saw a girl and a boy who looked sad and dirty. They had no toys and no shoes. They were sitting under a tree with their mom, who had a blanket around her.

"Who are they, mom?" Anna asked.

"They are a family who have no home, no money, and no food," mom said. "They are very poor."

"Why are they poor, mom?" Ben asked.

"Because life is not fair, Ben. Some people have more than they need, and some people have less than they need. But we can help them, if we want to."

"How can we help them, mom?" Anna asked.

"We can share some of our things with them, and we can pray for them. Praying means talking to God and asking him to help them and love them."

Anna and Ben nodded. They ran to their mom's car and brought back some of their toys and books and clothes. They gave them to the girl and the boy, who smiled and thanked them. They also gave them some of their snacks and water.

"Can we pray with them, mom?" Ben asked.

"Of course, Ben. Let's pray together." Mom said.

They all held hands and closed their eyes. Mom said, "Dear God, thank you for this day and for this park and for these children. Please help them and their mom to find a home, a job, and food. Please protect them and bless them. Please make them happy and healthy. And please help us to be kind and generous to everyone. Amen."

"Amen," Anna and Ben said.

They opened their eyes and hugged the girl and the boy. They played with them for a while, and then they said goodbye.

"Thank you for being our friends," the girl said.

"Thank you for being our friends, too," Anna said.

"Maybe we will see you again," the boy said.

"Maybe we will," Ben said.

They waved and got in their mom's car. They drove away, feeling happy and grateful. They learned that being wealthy is not only having many things, but also sharing them with others. And they learned that praying is a way of showing love and care.

"Sure, sweeties. There is a jug of milk in the fridge. You can pour some in your cups and then go to your beds. I will come and tuck you in soon." Mom said.

Sam and Lily went to the kitchen and saw the jug of milk on the shelf. They tried to reach it, but it was too high. They got a chair and climbed on it. Sam grabbed the jug and tried to pull it down. But it was too heavy and slippery. The jug fell from his hands and crashed on the floor. Milk splashed everywhere. Sam and Lily screamed.

Mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw the mess and the broken jug. She was very angry and sad.

"What have you done? You made a big mess and wasted the milk. You could have hurt yourselves. You are very naughty and careless. You will not get any milk or nap today. You will have to clean up and stay in the corner." Mom said.

Sam and Lily cried and said they were sorry. But Mom did not listen. She gave them a mop and a bucket and told them to start cleaning. Sam and Lily felt very tired and thirsty. They wished they had listened to Mom and not touched the jug. They had a bad day.

He saw a man walking by with a suit and a hat. The man looked very busy and important. Tom thought the man's suit was nice and shiny. He wanted to try it on.

Tom sneaked out from behind the tree and followed the man. He waited until the man sat on a bench and put his hat and suit on the ground. Tom quickly grabbed the hat and suit and ran away. He put them on and looked at himself. He felt very fine and smart. He did not see Lily looking for him.

Lily searched everywhere for Tom. She could not find him. She was sad and worried. She thought Tom was lost or hurt. She asked some people if they saw Tom, but they said no. She saw a man with a suit and a hat walking by. She did not know it was Tom. She thought the man was a stranger. She was scared of him.

The man saw Lily and smiled. He said, "Hello, Lily. Do you like my suit and hat?" Lily was surprised. She recognized Tom's voice. She said, "Tom, is that you? Why are you wearing that suit and hat? They are not yours. They belong to someone else. You should give them back. That is not nice. That is stealing."

Tom felt ashamed. He realized he did something wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I wanted to look fine and smart. I did not think about the man. I did not think about you. I was selfish and silly. Please forgive me." He took off the suit and hat and ran back to the bench. He saw the man looking for his suit and hat. He said, "I'm sorry, sir. I took your suit and hat. Here they are. Please don't be angry. I won't do it again." The man was surprised and annoyed. He said, "Thank you for returning them, but you should not have taken them in the first place. That was very rude and dishonest. You should respect other people's things. You should be happy with what you have. You should be yourself."

Tom nodded. He said, "You are right, sir. I learned my lesson. I don't need a suit and hat to be fine and smart. I have my own clothes and my own personality. I have my friend Lily who likes me for who I am. I'm sorry for making her sad and worried. I'm sorry for making you angry. I hope you have a good day." The man said, "I accept your apology, but don't do it again. I hope you have a good day too." He put on his suit and hat and walked away.

"Hello, caterpillar," Anna said. "Do you want to be my friend?"

The caterpillar did not say anything. It just munched on the leaf.

Anna picked up the caterpillar gently. She was careful not to hurt it. She knew it was delicate. She put it on her hand and stroked it softly.

"Come with me, caterpillar," Anna said. "I will show you my toys and my books. We will have fun together."

The caterpillar did not want to go with Anna. It wanted to stay on the leaf. It wanted to eat and grow and make a cocoon. It tried to wiggle off Anna's hand.

"No, caterpillar, don't go," Anna said. "Please stay with me. I insist. You are my friend."

The caterpillar did not listen to Anna. It crawled off her hand and back to the leaf. It was not happy with Anna. It was scared and annoyed.

Anna was sad and angry. She did not understand why the caterpillar did not want to be her friend. She cried and stomped her feet.

"Mommy, mommy," Anna called. "The caterpillar is mean. It does not want to play with me. It ran away from me."

Mommy came to the garden. She saw Anna and the caterpillar. She hugged Anna and wiped her tears.

"Anna, sweetheart, the caterpillar is not mean," Mommy said. "It is just different from you. It has its own life and needs. It does not want to play with toys or books. It wants to eat and sleep and change. It is not a good friend for you. You need to let it go and find another friend. Maybe a butterfly or a bird or a dog."

Anna looked at the caterpillar. She saw that it was busy and happy on the leaf. She felt sorry for bothering it. She said sorry to the caterpillar.

"Sorry, caterpillar," Anna said. "I did not mean to make you sad or scared. I hope you have a good life. Goodbye, caterpillar."

Anna let go of the caterpillar. She smiled and waved at it. She thanked Mommy for helping her. She went to look for another friend in the garden. She hoped to find a butterfly or a bird or a dog. She knew they would be more fun and friendly than a caterpillar.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to play in the farm. They saw a chicken coop with many chickens inside. They wanted to catch a chicken and take it home.

"Let's plan how to get a chicken," Tom said. "We can wait until the farmer is away and then sneak in."

Sam nodded. He thought it was a good plan. They hid behind a hay bale and watched the farmer. When the farmer went inside his house, they ran to the chicken coop.

They opened the door and tried to grab a chicken. But the chickens were scared and noisy. They flapped their wings and pecked at Tom and Sam. Tom and Sam got hurt and dropped the chicken.

The farmer heard the commotion and came out. He saw Tom and Sam with feathers in their hair and scratches on their arms. He was angry and shouted at them.

"What are you doing here? You are not allowed to touch my chickens! They are not yours! They are mine! You are bad boys!"

Tom and Sam felt sorry and ashamed. They apologized to the farmer and ran away. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should not take what is not theirs. They learned that chickens are not toys. They learned that the farmer was harsh but fair.

"Look at me, Lily!" Ben says. "I can grab the tire with one hand!"

He lets go of one hand and holds on to the tire with the other. He feels very brave and wild.

But then he loses his grip and falls off the tire. He lands on the grass with a thud.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cries. "That hurt!"

Lily runs to him and helps him get up. She sees that he has a scrape on his knee and a tear in his pants.

"Are you okay, Ben?" she asks. "You were too wild. You should be careful."

Ben nods and wipes his eyes. He is sorry that he was too wild. He hugs Lily and says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend."

They walk to the bench where their moms are sitting. They get some water and a band-aid for Ben's knee. They decide to play something else that is not so wild. Maybe they can slide or build a sandcastle. They still have fun in the park.

Tom and Sue are friends who like to play on the beach. They have a big boat made of sand and shells. They pretend to sail to faraway lands and have adventures.

One day, they find a real anchor on the shore. It is heavy and rusty and has a long rope. They think it is a treasure from a pirate ship. They want to take it to their boat, but it is too hard to drag.

They try to think of a way to solve their problem. They look around and see a big cart with wheels. It belongs to a man who sells ice cream. He is busy talking to some customers. Tom and Sue decide to borrow his cart for a little while.

They lift the anchor and put it on the cart. They push the cart to their boat. They tie the rope to the boat and pretend the anchor is keeping them safe from storms and sharks. They are very happy and proud.

The ice cream man sees them and walks over. He is not angry, but he wants his cart back. He asks them what they are doing with his anchor. Tom and Sue tell him their story. He laughs and says he found the anchor in a junkyard and uses it as a weight to keep his cart steady.

He says they can keep the anchor if they want, but they have to return his cart. He also gives them each a tasty ice cream cone as a reward for their creativity. Tom and Sue thank him and enjoy their ice cream. They decide to share their anchor with their other friends and have more fun on the beach.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a shiny silver ball in their toy box. They both wanted to play with it, but there was only one ball.

"Give me the ball, Lily!" Tom said. "I saw it first!"

"No, Tom, I want the ball!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and round!"

They pulled and tugged at the ball, but neither of them would let go. They started to yell and cry, and their mom heard them.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked. "Why are you fighting over a ball?"

"Mom, Tom is trying to take the ball from me!" Lily said.

"Mom, Lily is trying to take the ball from me!" Tom said.

Mom looked at the ball and shook her head. "This is not a toy, children. This is a silver ornament that belongs to Grandma. She gave it to me to keep it safe. It is very old and fragile, and you could break it if you are not careful."

Tom and Lily felt sorry for what they had done. They did not know that the ball was not a toy, and that it was special to Mom and Grandma. They let go of the ball and hugged each other.

"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We did not mean to be bad. We just wanted to play with the ball."

Mom smiled and hugged them back. "I know, children. But you should not fight over things, even if they are toys. You should share and take turns, and be kind to each other. That is what makes you happy and jolly, not what you have."

Tom and Lily nodded and agreed. They learned their lesson, and decided to play with their other toys instead. They also promised to be more careful with Grandma's silver ball, and to ask Mom before they touched anything that was not theirs. Mom was proud of them, and gave them each a kiss. They were a jolly family again.

Tom was a bad boy. He did not listen to his mom and dad. He liked to play with things that were not his. One day, he saw a nurse's bag in the park. He wanted to see what was inside. He ran to the bag and lifted it.

"Hey, that's mine!" a voice said. Tom turned and saw a nurse. She looked angry. She was wearing a white coat and a hat with a red cross. She had a stethoscope around her neck.

"Give it back, please. I need it for my work. I help sick people," the nurse said.

Tom did not care. He wanted to keep the bag. He ran away with it. The nurse chased him. She was faster than Tom. She caught him and took the bag from him.

"That was very bad of you. You should not take things that are not yours. You could have hurt someone who needed my help. How would you feel if someone took your toys?" the nurse said.

Tom felt ashamed. He realized he was wrong. He looked at the nurse and said, "I'm sorry. I was bad. I won't do it again. Please forgive me."

The nurse smiled. She was kind. She said, "I forgive you. But you have to promise me to be good from now on. And you have to say sorry to your mom and dad, too. They must be worried about you."

Tom nodded. He said, "I promise. I will say sorry to them. And I will be good. Thank you, nurse."

The nurse hugged him. She said, "You're welcome. Now, let's go find your mom and dad. They must be looking for you."

Tom and the nurse walked back to the park. They found Tom's mom and dad. Tom ran to them and hugged them. He said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I was bad. I took a nurse's bag. But she forgave me. And I learned my lesson. I will be good."

Tom's mom and dad were happy. They said, "We're glad you're safe. And we're proud of you for saying sorry and learning your lesson. But don't ever do that again. It's dangerous and wrong."

Tom said, "I won't. I love you, mom and dad."

They said, "We love you, too, Tom."

The nurse waved goodbye. She said, "Bye, Tom. Be good. And thank you for giving me back my bag."

Tom waved back. He said, "Bye, nurse. Thank you for being nice. And thank you for helping sick people."

The end.

Moral value: Do not take things that are not yours. It's bad and it can hurt others. Say sorry when you make a mistake and learn from it. Be good and kind.

But Ben is not so sure. He looks at his car and sees that it is wet and dripping. He thinks that water is not fuel. He thinks that water is for drinking and washing, not for cars.

"Water is not fuel," he says. "It is bad for cars. It makes them sick and rusty. We need real fuel."

Mia's car is not as fast as Sam's truck. But it can make loud noises. Mia presses a button and her car makes a siren sound. It sounds like a police car. Mia says, "Stop, stop, you are breaking the rules. You have to slow down or I will catch you."

Sam hears the siren and gets scared. He thinks Mia is a real police car. He says, "No, no, I am not breaking the rules. I am just racing. Please don't catch me."

He tries to speed up, but he is too close to the door. He can't stop his truck in time. He crashes into the door and falls off his truck. He hurts his head and his arm. He cries and says, "Ow, ow, that hurts. Help me, help me."

Mia stops her car and runs to Sam. She sees him crying and bleeding. She feels sorry for him. She says, "Oh, Sam, I am sorry. I was just playing. I didn't mean to scare you. Are you OK?"

Sam looks at Mia and shrugs. He says, "I don't know. I think I need a band-aid. And a hug. And maybe a new truck."

Mia hugs Sam and says, "I will get you a band-aid. And a hug. And maybe we can share my car. But next time, let's not race so fast. It's not fun to get hurt."

Sam nods and says, "OK, next time, let's not race so fast. It's not fun to get hurt. But can I still have a new truck?"

Mia sighs and says, "Maybe. But only if you are nice to me. And fair."

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sammy. Sammy loved to eat nuts. He would climb up trees to find the best nuts to eat. One day, Sammy found a fancy nut that was different from all the other nuts he had ever seen. 

Sammy wanted to eat the fancy nut, but he couldn't crack it open with his teeth. He tried and tried, but it wouldn't budge. Then, he had an idea. He ran to his friend, a wise old owl, and asked for help. 

The owl took one look at the fancy nut and knew what to do. He used his strong beak to crack it open. Inside, there was a surprise - the nut had changed into a shiny gold coin! Sammy was so happy and grateful to his friend. From that day on, he always shared his nuts with the wise old owl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her dolls. She had a favorite doll named Rosie who was her model for everything. One day, Lily's mom took Rosie away and put her on a high shelf. Lily asked, "Mommy, where is Rosie?" Her mom replied, "Rosie is suffering from a little cold. She needs to rest and get better."

Lily didn't understand what "suffer" meant, so she asked, "What does 'suffer' mean?" Her mom explained, "It means Rosie doesn't feel good and needs to rest until she feels better." Lily felt sad for her doll and said, "I hope Rosie feels better soon."

A few days later, Rosie was feeling better and Lily was happy to have her back. She realized that she was ignorant about what "suffer" meant before, but now she knew it meant when someone or something doesn't feel good. From then on, Lily made sure to take good care of her dolls so they wouldn't suffer.

One day, she saw a rich girl named Mia. Mia had a lot of clothes and toys. She always wore shiny dresses and shoes. She had a big doll that could talk and sing. Lila wanted to have a doll like that. She went to Mia and said, "Hi, Mia. I like your doll. Can I play with it?"

Mia looked at Lila and said, "No, you can't. This is my doll. You have nothing to play with. You have ugly clothes and no toys. Go away, you are poor and dirty."

Lila felt sad and angry. She ran away and cried. She wished she could sell her old clothes and buy a new doll. She thought Mia was mean and rude.

The next day, Lila saw a boy named Ben. Ben had no clothes and no toys. He lived on the street and had no mom or dad. He was cold and hungry. He saw Lila and said, "Hi, Lila. I like your clothes. Can I have them?"

Lila looked at Ben and said, "Yes, you can. These are my clothes. You have nothing to wear. You have no home and no food. Here, take my clothes. They will keep you warm and cozy."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lila. You are very kind and generous. You have a big heart and a good soul. You are my friend."

Lila felt happy and proud. She gave Ben her old clothes and hugged him. She did not need a new doll. She had a new friend. She thought Ben was sweet and nice.

The moral of the story is: You don't need to have a lot of things to be happy. You need to have a lot of love and kindness. You should not judge people by their looks or their money. You should judge them by their actions and their words.

It was a rainy day and Anna wanted to go outside and play. She put on her boots and coat and took her umbrella. She saw her friend Ben across the street. He was holding a big cardboard box.

"Hi, Ben! What do you have in your box?" Anna asked.

"Hi, Anna! I have a surprise for you. Come and see!" Ben said.

Anna ran across the street and looked inside the box. She saw a puppet made of socks and buttons. It had a funny face and a red hat.

"Wow, Ben! That is a great puppet! Did you make it?" Anna said.

"Yes, I did. His name is Bobo. He can talk and sing and dance. Do you want to see a show?" Ben said.

"Yes, please!" Anna said.

Ben took out Bobo and put him on his hand. He made a funny voice and moved Bobo around. He made Bobo say hello to Anna and tell jokes. He made Bobo sing a song and dance on the box. Anna laughed and clapped her hands. She liked the show very much.

"Bravo, Ben! Bravo, Bobo! That was a wonderful show!" Anna said.

"Thank you, Anna! Thank you for being my friend!" Ben said.

They hugged and smiled. They were very happy.

But then they heard a loud voice. It was Ben's big brother, Tom. He was coming home from school. He saw Ben and Anna and the puppet show. He was very angry.

"Hey, Ben! What are you doing with that stupid puppet? That is so babyish! You should be ashamed of yourself!" Tom said.

He grabbed the box and threw it in the trash. He took Bobo and ripped him apart. He threw the pieces on the ground. He laughed and walked away.

Ben and Anna were very sad. They looked at the broken puppet and the empty box. They felt like crying.

"Ben, I'm so sorry. Tom is very mean. He should be ashamed of himself!" Anna said.

"It's okay, Anna. Don't be sad. Bobo was just a puppet. He was not real. But you are real. You are my friend. And you liked my show. That makes me happy." Ben said.

He took Anna's hand and gave her a smile. He took her umbrella and opened it. He put it over their heads.

"Come on, Anna. Let's go and play. The rain is fun. We can splash and jump and make rainbows. We can make our own show. And we can applaud each other. Because we are friends." Ben said.

Anna nodded and smiled. She squeezed Ben's hand and followed him. They ran and played and had fun. They forgot about Tom and Bobo. They were not ashamed. They were proud. They were friends.

Lily and Ben did not think the lemonade was good for them. They thought it was bad for them. They wanted something sweet and cold.

Tom was a restless boy who liked to question everything. He always asked his mom and dad why the sky was blue, why the grass was green, why the sun was hot, and so on. Sometimes they had answers, sometimes they did not.

One day, Tom found a big book in his dad's study. It had many strange words and pictures on it. Tom was curious and opened the book. He saw a word that looked like this: A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A. He wondered what it meant.

He ran to his mom and showed her the book. "Mom, what is this word?" he asked.

Mom looked at the book and smiled. "That is a spell, Tom. It is a word that some people use to do magic. But you have to be careful with spells. They can be good or bad."

Tom was amazed. He wanted to do magic. He asked his mom, "Can I say the spell, Mom? Can I do magic?"

Mom shook her head. "No, Tom. You are too young to say spells. You don't know what they can do. Maybe they can make things disappear, or change, or fly. Maybe they can make you happy, or sad, or scared. You have to be very careful with spells. They are not for playing."

Tom was disappointed. He wanted to try the spell. He thought his mom was just being mean. He decided to wait until his mom was busy and then say the spell. He thought it would be fun.

He hid the book under his bed and waited for his mom to go to the kitchen. When she did, he took the book and ran to the backyard. He looked around and saw a big tree. He thought it would be cool to make the tree fly. He opened the book and found the spell. He said it out loud: "A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A!"

Suddenly, the tree shook and lifted off the ground. Tom was shocked and happy. He had done magic! He laughed and clapped his hands. He said the spell again and again, making the tree go higher and higher.

But then, something went wrong. The tree stopped flying and started falling. It was falling fast and hard. It was falling towards Tom. Tom was scared and sorry. He had done a bad spell. He wanted to stop it. He tried to say the spell backwards, but he could not remember it. He screamed for his mom.

Mom heard Tom's scream and ran to the backyard. She saw the tree falling and Tom in danger. She was scared and angry. She grabbed Tom and pulled him away from the tree. The tree crashed to the ground, making a loud noise and a big mess.

Mom hugged Tom and checked if he was hurt. He was not, but he was crying. He was sorry for what he had done. He told his mom he had said the spell and made the tree fly and fall. He said he was sorry and he would never say spells again.

Mom was relieved and glad that Tom was safe. She was also sad and mad that Tom had disobeyed her and used the book. She told Tom he had been very naughty and foolish. She told him he had to go to his room and think about what he had done. She told him he had to give back the book and never touch it again.

Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He gave back the book and went to his room. He felt bad and scared. He wished he had listened to his mom. He learned that spells were not for playing. He learned that questioning everything was not always good. He learned that being restless could get him in trouble. He decided to be a good boy from now on. He decided to be more careful with words. He decided to be more happy with what he had. He decided to be more thankful for his mom. He decided to say a different word: "I love you, Mom."

One day, Lily was walking in the park when she saw a man who was deaf. She wanted to talk to him, but she didn't know how. She went up to him and said, "Hi! I'm Lily. Can you hear me?" The man smiled and said, "No, I can't hear you, but I can see you. You're very kind to come say hello."

Lily was happy that she made a new friend and protected the little bird. She knew that being kind and helpful to others was the most important thing, even if they were different from her.

Later that day, Lily went to the park with her dad. They played on the swings and went down the slide. But when it was time to go home, Lily couldn't get her grip off the swing. Her dad told her to release her hands and she did. She felt happy and proud that she did it all by herself. 

When they got home, Lily's mom made her spaghetti with sauce again. Lily smiled and said, "I released the swing and the sauce spilled, but it's okay because accidents happen." Her parents were proud of her for using the word "release" and for being so brave at the park. They all enjoyed their dinner together. The end.

The bird replied, "I whistle because I am happy. I may be poor, but I still have the river and its music."

The bird kept drinking from the river, and whistling its happy song. Now whenever the fisherman passes by the river, he always takes a moment to stop and listen to the singing of the poor bird.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Lily and Max. They liked to play together every day. One day, they found a toy car in the park. Lily wanted to play with it, but Max wanted to play with it too. They started to disagree and argue about who could play with it.

Lily said, "I found it first, so I get to play with it!" Max said, "No, I want to play with it too. Let's share it!" But they couldn't agree on what to do. They both wanted to play with the toy car, but only one of them could play with it at a time.

Then, Lily had an idea. She said, "Let's take turns playing with it. I'll play with it first, and then you can play with it after me." Max thought that was a good idea, so they decided to take turns. They were careful not to fight anymore and they enjoyed playing with the toy car together.

The moral of the story is that when you disagree with someone, it's important to find a solution that makes everyone happy. It's also important to be careful with your words and actions, and to think about how your actions might affect others. And lastly, it's important to share and take turns, so that everyone can have fun.

Sara looked at Tom. He looked sad and sorry. She remembered that he was her brother and that she loved him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I should not have shouted at you. You can play with my paint and my brush sometimes, if you ask me. And I can play with your cars sometimes, if you ask me."
