She grabs her car and runs to the door. Sam runs after her and tries to stop her.

"Mia, wait!" he says. "Don't go! Don't take your car!"

But Mia does not listen. She opens the door and runs outside. Sam follows her, but he is too late. Mia is already in the rain, zooming her car on the wet grass. She laughs and smiles. She does not see the big puddle in front of her. She zooms her car right into it. The car sinks and disappears. Mia gasps and cries.

"Sam, help!" she says. "My car is gone!"

Sam runs to her and hugs her. He feels sorry for her. He knows how much she loves her car.

"I'm sorry, Mia," he says. "I tried to tell you. The rain is not for our cars. It is for the plants and the birds and the worms. Maybe we can find your car later, when the rain stops. But now, let's go inside and play with my car. We can share it and make zoom sounds and race it on the floor. Okay?"

Mia nods and wipes her tears. She is still sad, but she is also glad that Sam is her brother. He is kind and generous. He shares his car with her and makes her feel better.

They go inside and play with Sam's car. They make zoom sounds and race it on the floor. They pretend the car is in a big city or a jungle or a desert. They forget about the rain and have fun.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a farm. They liked to help their dad with the animals and the crops. One day, their dad told them he had a surprise for them. He took them to the barn and showed them a big, shiny tractor.

"This is a famous tractor," their dad said. "It belonged to a great farmer who won many prizes. He gave it to me as a gift, and now I want to share it with you. You can take turns to drive it, but you have to be careful and follow the rules."

Ben and Sam were very excited. They wanted to drive the famous tractor right away. Ben went first. He climbed on the seat and started the engine. He drove around the field, feeling very proud. He saw Sam waiting by the barn, and he waved at him.

"Can I have a turn now?" Sam asked.

"Wait a little more," Ben said. "I'm not done yet."

Ben drove for a long time, and Sam got bored. He decided to sit on the tractor's wheel and play with a stick. He did not see that Ben was coming back. Ben did not see him either. He was too busy looking at the sky and the trees.

Crash! The tractor hit Sam and knocked him off the wheel. Sam fell to the ground and cried out in pain. Ben stopped the tractor and ran to him. He saw that Sam had a big cut on his leg and blood on his clothes.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" Ben said. "I didn't see you! Are you okay?"

Sam was not okay. He was hurt and angry. He pushed Ben away and said, "You're mean! You didn't let me have a turn! You're selfish!"

Their dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. He saw Sam's wound and Ben's tears. He took Sam to the house and bandaged his leg. He told Ben to sit on the porch and think about what he did.

Ben felt very bad. He knew he was wrong. He wished he had shared the tractor with Sam. He wished he had paid attention to where he was going. He wished he could say sorry to Sam and make him feel better.

He sat on the porch for a long time, until he saw Sam coming out of the house. Sam walked slowly, with a limp. He looked sad and tired. Ben got up and ran to him. He hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry I was mean and selfish. I'm sorry I hurt you. Can you forgive me?"

Sam looked at Ben and saw that he was sincere. He felt his anger melt away. He hugged him back and said, "I forgive you, Ben. I'm sorry I was mad at you. You're my brother, and I love you."

Their dad saw them and smiled. He was glad they made up. He said, "Boys, I'm proud of you. You learned a valuable lesson today. The famous tractor is not as important as your friendship. Sharing and caring are more important than having and keeping. And always watch where you're going, especially when you're driving a big, shiny tractor."

Lily frowns. She wants Ben to join her. She thinks diving is easy and fun. She has an idea. She swims to the edge of the pool and gets out. She runs to the bench where their clothes are. She picks up Ben's shirt and pants and throws them into the water.

"Hey!" Ben shouts. "What are you doing? Those are my clothes!"

Lily laughs. "Now you have to dive to get them! Come on, it's not hard. I'll help you."

Ben is angry and sad. He doesn't want to dive. He doesn't want his clothes to get wet. He doesn't think Lily is funny. He thinks she is mean. He starts to cry.

Lily sees Ben's tears and feels sorry. She realizes she made a mistake. She dives into the water and gets Ben's clothes. She brings them back to him and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was just joking. I didn't mean to make you cry. Here are your clothes. They are not too wet. You can dry them in the sun."

Ben stops crying and takes his clothes. He looks at Lily and says, "Thank you, Lily. I'm sorry I was scared. Maybe I can try to dive with you next time. But please don't throw my clothes again."

Lily nods and hugs Ben. She says, "OK, Ben. I won't do that again. I'm sorry I was mean. You are my friend. I like to play with you."

Ben smiles and hugs Lily back. He says, "You are my friend too. I like to play with you too."

They go back to the pool and play together. They splash and swim and have fun. Sometimes Lily dives and sometimes Ben watches. They are happy.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with shiny things. One day, they found a big copper pot in the yard. It was old and dirty, but they thought it was a treasure.

They took the pot to their room and tried to clean it. They used water, soap, and a brush. But the pot was still brown and dull. They were sad.

Then, Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's use mom's polish. It will make the pot shiny and bright." Sam agreed. They sneaked into the kitchen and took the polish and a cloth.

They went back to their room and rubbed the polish on the pot. The pot started to shine. They were happy. They thanked each other for the idea.

But they did not know that the polish was not for copper. It was for silver. It had a bad smell and a bad taste. It made the pot poisonous.

The next day, mom made soup for lunch. She did not have a big pot, so she used the copper pot that Tom and Sam had polished. She did not see the polish on it. She filled it with water, vegetables, and meat. She cooked it on the stove.

She called Tom and Sam to eat. They came to the table and saw the soup. It looked good. They did not know it was bad. They took a spoon and tasted it.

They felt sick. They coughed and choked. They fell on the floor. Mom saw them and screamed. She called for help. But it was too late. Tom and Sam were dead.

They were foolish. They should not have used the polish. They should have asked mom first. They paid a big price for their shiny pot.

At the park, they saw lions, elephants, monkeys, and many other animals. They wanted to see them all, but they had to stay close to their mom and dad. Sometimes they heard the animals make loud noises, like roar, trumpet, or chatter. They were curious and excited.

One day, they saw a sign that said "Unknown Animal". They wondered what it was. They asked their mom and dad, but they said they didn't know either. They said it was a surprise and they had to wait until the next day to find out.

Tim and Kim were very impatient. They wanted to see the unknown animal right away. When their mom and dad were busy talking to a guide, they sneaked away and followed the sign. They walked for a long time until they reached a big cage.

Inside the cage, they saw a strange animal. It had a long neck, a big head, and spots all over its body. It looked like a mix of a horse and a giraffe. They had never seen anything like it before. They thought it was amazing.

They went closer to the cage and tried to talk to the animal. They said hello and asked its name. The animal looked at them and opened its mouth. It made a loud noise that sounded like a roar and a neigh. Tim and Kim were scared. They ran away as fast as they could.

They ran back to their mom and dad, who were very worried and angry. They asked them where they had been and why they had left them. Tim and Kim told them about the unknown animal and how it had roared at them. They said they were sorry and that they had learned their lesson.

Their mom and dad hugged them and said they were glad they were safe. They said the unknown animal was called an okapi and that it was very rare and shy. They said they should never go away from them without permission and that they should always respect the animals and their space.

Tim and Kim nodded and said they understood. They said they still liked the okapi and wanted to see it again, but only with their mom and dad. They said they loved the park and the animals and the holiday. They said they loved their mom and dad too.

The people in the town were happy to see the nosy judge having fun with them. They all danced, ate cake, and laughed together. From that day on, the judge was not so nosy anymore. He learned that it was more fun to celebrate with his friends.

One day, a cat and a dog went to a stage to play. The cat was rude and did not want to share the toys. The dog tried to resist being sad but he could not. He asked the cat, "Can we play together, please?"

The cat said, "No, these are my toys. Go away!" The dog felt bad and walked away. The sky turned dark and it began to rain. The dog looked back at the stage and saw the cat still playing alone.

The rain got heavier and the stage started to flood. The cat got scared and called out to the dog, "Help me, please!" But the dog was too far away to hear the cat. The cat was stuck on the stage and the rain did not stop. The cat learned that being rude was not good.

The storm passed, and the sun came out again. Bobby was safe and dry because he shut his door. The other boats were wet and sad. They learned that it's important to listen and do what they're told. Bobby and his friends played happily in the harbor again, and they always remembered to shut their doors when a storm came.

Finn had an idea. He used his strong tail to pull the wire off Bob. "Now you can sail, Bob!" said Finn. Bob was very happy. He sailed away, waving goodbye to his new friend Finn.

His mum replied, "No, Jack. Comets aren't for people to ride on, but I can allow you to look at it."

Jack was relieved and smiled. He liked the comet and was happy that he was allowed to look at it in the night sky.

Once upon a time, there was a brown bear. The bear had a very long neck, and he loved to stretch it out and look at the world around him.

One day, the bear noticed something in the sky - a little bee. The bee was buzzing around, and the bear thought it looked beautiful. But then, the bee accidentally flew too close to the bear's neck and the bear became very scared. He began to growl and swat at the bee.

But the bee just hovered in the air, looking at the bear. It knew the bear was not really mad, and it was just scared. So the bee buzzed softly, and said "Please forgive me, I did not mean to scare you."

The bear stopped swatting and listened. Slowly he understand that the bee was sorry for scaring him, and he knew he should forgive it. He nudged his head gently and said "Yes, I forgive you" and the two of them smiled and flew away together.

As they were fishing, a big wave came and hit their boat. The boat tipped over and they fell into the water. Timmy's dad tried to swim but he couldn't. Timmy was too little to help him. They were stuck in the deep water and couldn't get out. They were scared and cold. 

Sadly, no one could find them and they never came back home. Timmy's mom was very sad and missed them very much. She would always remember the happy times they had at the beach.

But when she looked around, she couldn't find them anywhere. She started to feel sad because she missed her friends. She looked behind trees, under bushes, and even in the pond, but her friends were nowhere to be seen. Just when she was about to give up, she heard a giggle coming from behind a big rock. It was her friends! They had been hiding there the whole time. 

Lily was so happy to have found her friends and they all played together until it was time to go home. As she walked back to her house, she thought about how much fun she had and how much she would miss her friends until they played again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she was playing with her friend Max when she saw a rare bird in the sky.

"Look, Max! A rare bird!" Lily exclaimed.

Max looked up and saw the bird too. "Wow, that's amazing! Can we reach it?" he asked.

Lily shook her head. "No, the bird is too high up in the sky. But we can try to draw it on our shirts!"

Max smiled and they both ran inside to get their shirts and markers. They spent the rest of the day drawing pictures of the rare bird and having fun together. When Lily's mom saw their shirts, she was so impressed that she took a picture of them to show her friends.

Lily and Max were proud of their artwork and couldn't wait to show it off to everyone they knew. They learned that even if they couldn't reach the rare bird in the sky, they could still capture its beauty in their own way.

Later that day, the bear saw a tree that had fallen over and was blocking the path for all the animals. The bear tried to lift the tree with his strong shoulder, but it was too heavy. Tom and Lily held hands and looked at the mountain. They imagined what it was like to be on the mountain. They thought it was cold and snowy and windy. They thought it was beautiful and exciting and fun.

They smiled and hugged each other. They were happy to have each other and to see the mountain. They said they would always remember the mountain and their mom. They said they loved them very much.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. But today, the park is very cold and wet. The sky is pale and gray. The wind is strong and loud.

"Mom, can we go home?" Sara asks. She shivers and hugs her teddy bear. "I don't like the park today. It is too cold and wet."

"Not yet, Sara. We have to wait for the bus. The bus will take us home." Mom says. She puts her scarf around Sara's neck. "Look, there is a wide slide. Do you want to try it?"

"No, thank you. The slide is wet and slippery. I might fall and hurt myself." Sara says. She complains and pouts.

Ben is not afraid of the slide. He runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. He smiles and waves at Mom and Sara. "Look at me! I'm going to slide down the wide slide. Whee!" He shouts.

He slides down the slide very fast. He laughs and enjoys the ride. But when he reaches the bottom, he splashes into a big puddle. He gets wet and muddy. He gasps and cries.

"Mom, help! I'm wet and muddy. I don't like the slide. It is too wet and slippery. I want to go home." He says.

Mom runs to Ben and picks him up. She wipes his face and clothes with a tissue. She hugs him and comforts him. "It's okay, Ben. You had fun on the slide. But now you are wet and muddy. We will go home soon. The bus is coming. See?" She points to the bus.

Sara and Ben see the bus. They stop complaining and crying. They follow Mom to the bus. They get on the bus and sit on the seats. They look out the window and see the park. They say goodbye to the park. They hope the park will be sunny and dry tomorrow. They want to play in the park again. But not on the wide slide.

Lily and Max were going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They were going to fly on a big plane to see Grandma and Grandpa. Lily was very excited, but Max was nervous. He had never flown on a plane before.

"Max, why are you so quiet?" Lily asked her brother. "Don't you want to go on vacation?"

"I do, but I'm scared of the plane," Max said. "What if it goes too fast, or too high, or makes a loud noise?"

Lily hugged Max and said, "Don't worry, Max. The plane is safe and fun. Mom and Dad will be with us, and they will help us. And when we get to Grandma and Grandpa's house, we will have a lot of fun. We can play with their dog, and bake cookies, and read stories."

Max smiled a little and said, "OK, Lily. I will try to be brave. But can you hold my hand when we get on the plane?"

"Of course, Max. I will always hold your hand," Lily said.

They packed their bags and got in the car. Mom and Dad drove them to the airport. They checked in their bags and got their tickets. They walked to the gate, where they saw the big plane. Max felt his heart beat faster. He squeezed Lily's hand.

"Are you ready, Max?" Lily asked.

Max nodded and said, "Yes, Lily. I'm ready. Let's go on vacation."

They followed Mom and Dad and boarded the plane. They found their seats and buckled their belts. The plane started to move and then to change. It went faster and faster, and then it lifted off the ground. Max closed his eyes and held Lily's hand tighter.

"It's OK, Max. We're flying," Lily said. "Look out the window. You can see the clouds and the sun."

Max opened his eyes and looked out the window. He saw the blue sky and the white clouds. He saw the ground get smaller and smaller. He felt the plane go up and down and sideways. He heard the engine roar and the wind whistle. He felt a strange feeling in his stomach.

He looked at Lily and said, "Lily, this is amazing. I'm not scared anymore. I like flying."

Lily smiled and said, "I'm glad, Max. I like flying too. We're going to have a great vacation."

They leaned back in their seats and enjoyed the ride. They talked and laughed and sang and played. They changed from nervous to happy. They were on vacation.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the forest. They liked to see the birds, the flowers and the trees. They liked to run, jump and hide. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw a big truck in the forest. The truck had a loud noise and a big saw. The truck was cutting down the trees. Ben and Lily were scared and sad.

They ran to the truck and shouted, "Stop! Stop! You are hurting the forest! The forest is good! The forest is our friend!"

The man in the truck heard them and stopped. He looked at them and said, "Why are you here? This is my job. I have to cut down the trees. I have to increase the wood for the people."

Ben and Lily said, "But the forest is not only for the people. The forest is for the animals, the plants and the air. The forest is good for everyone. If you cut down the trees, you will make the forest sick and small. Please, don't do it."

The man in the truck thought for a while. He said, "You are right. The forest is good for everyone. I don't want to hurt the forest. I will find another job. I will help the forest grow and be happy."

Ben and Lily smiled and said, "Thank you! Thank you! You are good too! You are our friend!"

They hugged the man and the truck. They waved goodbye and ran back to the forest. They played with the birds, the flowers and the trees. They had a lot of fun.

Jenny was a little girl who liked to do many things. She liked to draw, to sing, to play with her toys and to help her mom. But there was one thing she did not like to do: to go to the doctor.

The doctor was an elderly man who wore a white coat and a stethoscope. He was kind and gentle, but he sometimes had to use a needle to give Jenny a shot. Jenny was afraid of the needle, because it hurt and made her cry.

One day, Jenny had to go to the doctor for a check-up. She did not want to go, but her mom said it was important for her health. Jenny held her mom's hand and walked to the doctor's office. She saw the doctor smiling at her and said hello.

"Hello, Jenny," the doctor said. "How are you today?"

"I'm fine, thank you," Jenny said politely, but she felt nervous.

"That's good. Now, let me listen to your heart and lungs, and then we'll be done. Don't worry, it won't hurt a bit," the doctor said, as he put his stethoscope on Jenny's chest and back.

Jenny felt the cold metal on her skin and tried to be brave. She heard the doctor say, "Good, good, very good. You have a strong heart and clear lungs, Jenny. You are a healthy girl."

Jenny smiled and felt relieved. She thought the doctor was done, but then she saw him take out a needle from a drawer.

"What's that for?" Jenny asked, feeling scared.

"This is a shot, Jenny. It's a little pinch that will protect you from getting sick. It's very important, and it will be over soon. I promise," the doctor said, as he prepared the needle.

Jenny did not like the sound of that. She did not want a shot. She did not want a pinch. She wanted to go home. She started to cry and said, "No, no, no, please, no!"

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Jenny. I know you're scared, but the doctor is right. The shot will help you stay healthy and strong. It will only hurt for a second, and then it will be over. I'll be here with you. You can do it, Jenny. You're a brave girl."

Jenny looked at her mom and saw her love and care. She looked at the doctor and saw his kindness and patience. She took a deep breath and said, "Okay, okay, I'll do it. But only if you give me a sticker and a lollipop after."

The doctor smiled and said, "Deal. You're a smart girl, Jenny. Now, hold still and count to three. One, two, three."

Jenny felt the needle prick her arm and winced. She felt a tear roll down her cheek, but she did not scream. She counted to three and then it was over.

The doctor put a band-aid on her arm and said, "You did it, Jenny. You did very well. I'm proud of you. Here's your sticker and your lollipop. You can choose any color you want."

Jenny smiled and said, "Thank you, doctor. You're a nice man. I'm sorry I cried."

The doctor said, "You don't have to be sorry, Jenny. It's normal to cry when you're afraid or hurt. But you were very brave and strong. You did a great job."

Jenny hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Jenny. You're my brave girl."

Jenny felt happy and proud. She did something she did not like to do, but she did it anyway. She learned that sometimes doing things that are good for you can be hard, but they can also make you feel good. She learned that she had a strong heart and clear lungs, and a shot that would protect her from getting sick. She learned that she had a kind and gentle doctor, and a loving and caring mom. She learned that she was a healthy, smart and brave girl. And she learned that she liked stickers and lollipops.

"Let's cut a small piece, no one will notice," Ben said.

"Okay, but be careful," Lily said.

But Ben was not careful. He slipped and made a big cut in the cake. The cake fell on the floor and broke into pieces.

"Oh no, what have we done?" Lily cried.

"We have to repair it, quick!" Ben said.

They tried to put the cake back together, but it looked very bad. They used some frosting and sprinkles to cover the holes, but it was still messy. They put the cake back on the table and hoped no one would see it.

But their mom came home and saw the cake. She was very angry.

"Who did this to my cake?" she asked.

Ben and Lily felt guilty. They looked at each other and then at their mom.

"We did, mom, we're sorry," they said.

Mom sighed and hugged them.

"I'm glad you're honest, but you shouldn't touch things that are not yours. You could have hurt yourselves or made a bigger mess. Next time, ask me first if you want some cake, okay?"

"Okay, mom, we're sorry," they said.

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, I forgive you. But you have to help me make a new cake for my birthday, deal?"

"Deal, mom, we love you," they said.

They hugged mom and helped her make a new cake. It was not as big as the first one, but it was more delicious and they all enjoyed it. They learned their lesson and never touched mom's cake again.

But when he got closer, he heard a loud noise. It was a horn. The truck driver saw Tom and was angry. He did not want Tom to go near his truck. He shouted at Tom and honked his horn. Tom was scared and confused. He did not understand why the man was mad. He just wanted some beef.

Tom ran away from the truck and back to his yard. He was sad and hungry. He wished he had some beef. He did not know that the truck was not carrying beef, but cows. The cows were going to a place where they would become beef. Tom did not know that, and he was lucky that he did not find out.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big dog named Rex who was very obedient. He always listened to them and did what they said.

One day, they saw a new plant in the garden. It had green leaves and purple flowers. They smelled it and it was very nice.

"What is this?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a herb," Tom said.

"A herb? What is a herb?" Lily wondered.

"A herb is a plant that can make you healthy or tasty. Mommy uses herbs to cook sometimes," Tom explained.

"Wow, can we use this herb too?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask Mommy first," Tom said.

But Lily was too curious. She picked some of the leaves and put them in her mouth. She chewed them and made a face.

"Yuck! This herb is not tasty at all! It is bitter and spicy!" she cried.

She spit out the leaves and ran to the house. Tom followed her with Rex.

"Mommy, Mommy, I ate a herb and it was bad!" Lily said.

Mommy looked at her and saw that her mouth was red and swollen. She recognized the plant that Lily had eaten. It was not a herb, but a weed that could make people sick.

"Oh no, Lily, you ate a bad plant! You should not eat anything from the garden without asking me first. That plant can hurt you," Mommy said.

She took Lily to the bathroom and washed her mouth with water. She gave her some honey to soothe her throat. She hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily, you will be okay. But you have to be more careful next time."

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I was silly. I won't do it again," Lily said.

Tom and Rex came to the bathroom too. They felt sorry for Lily.

"Can we do something to help Lily, Mommy?" Tom asked.

"Yes, you can. You can pray for her. Praying is talking to God and asking him to help us. God loves us and he can make us feel better," Mommy said.

"Okay, Mommy. We will pray for Lily," Tom said.

He and Rex knelt down next to Lily and closed their eyes. They prayed for Lily to get well soon. They thanked God for Mommy and the garden and the good herbs. They asked God to forgive them for their mistakes and to teach them to be obedient.

Lily felt a warm feeling in her heart. She opened her eyes and smiled.

"Thank you, Tom. Thank you, Rex. Thank you, Mommy. Thank you, God. I love you all," she said.

"Yes, please," said the dog and the cat. "We want the ball, but the chain is too strong."

"I will win!" Lily says. She puts another block on her tower. But it is too heavy. Her tower falls down. The blocks make a loud noise.

"No, I will win!" Anna says. She puts another block on her tower. But it is too wobbly. Her tower falls down too. The blocks make another loud noise.

They both look at the mess. They feel sad. They did not win. They did not have fun.

They look at each other. They say sorry. They hug. They are sisters. They love each other.

They decide to play a different game. They play with dolls. They share. They laugh. They have fun. They are happy. They are both winners.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Anna has a new toy. It is a big, soft dog with a spot on its ear. Anna loves her new toy. She hugs it and says, "This is my spot dog. He is the best toy ever."

Ben sees Anna's spot dog. He wants it too. He thinks, "That is a nice toy. I wish I had a spot dog. Maybe Anna will let me play with it." He goes to Anna and says, "Can I play with your spot dog, please?"

Anna says, "No, this is my spot dog. He is mine. You have your own toys. Go away." She holds her spot dog tight and turns away from Ben.

Ben feels sad and angry. He thinks, "That is not fair. Anna is not a good friend. She does not share. I will take her spot dog when she is not looking." He waits for Anna to put down her spot dog. Then he runs and grabs it. He says, "Ha ha, now I have the spot dog. He is mine now."

Anna sees Ben take her spot dog. She cries and says, "Give me back my spot dog. You are a bad friend. You are a thief." She runs after Ben and tries to get her spot dog back.

They pull and tug on the spot dog. They yell and fight. The spot dog rips and tears. The stuffing comes out. The spot falls off. The spot dog is broken. Anna and Ben are both sad and sorry. They have no spot dog to play with. They have no friend to play with. They feel cold and lonely.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. If you share your toys, you will have more fun and more friends. If you are greedy and selfish, you will lose your toys and your friends. Be kind and generous, and you will receive happiness and love.

Tim and Sue liked to go to the bakery with their mom every Saturday. They saw many yummy things in the glass case, like cakes, pies, cookies, and pastries. Pastries were their favorite, because they were soft and sweet and had different fillings inside.

One day, they saw a new pastry that they had never seen before. It was round and brown and had white cream on top. They asked their mom what it was, and she said it was a donut. Tim and Sue wanted to try it, but their mom said they could only have one pastry each.

Tim and Sue had to discuss which pastry to choose. Tim liked the donut, because it looked fun and tasty. Sue liked the croissant, because it was flaky and buttery. They both thought the other pastry looked good too, but they could not agree on which one to share.

While they were discussing, they saw an elderly lady come into the bakery. She had gray hair and a kind smile. She walked slowly to the counter and asked for a donut. The baker gave her one and she paid with some coins. She looked very happy as she took a bite of her donut.

Tim and Sue watched the elderly lady and felt curious. They wondered why she liked the donut so much. They decided to ask her. They walked up to her and said hello. She smiled and said hello back. They asked her why she chose the donut. She said it was her favorite pastry, because it reminded her of her husband, who used to buy her one every Saturday. She said he was gone now, but she still came to the bakery to remember him.

Tim and Sue felt sad for the elderly lady, but also happy that she had a special memory. They said they were sorry for her loss, but also glad that she enjoyed the donut. They said they wanted to try the donut too, but they also liked the croissant. They asked her if she liked the croissant. She said she did, but she preferred the donut. She said they could have both, if they wanted. She reached into her purse and gave them some coins. She said it was a gift from her and her husband.

Tim and Sue thanked the elderly lady and hugged her. They ran to the counter and bought a donut and a croissant. They shared them with each other and with their mom. They said they were both delicious, but they liked the donut a little more. They said it was a special pastry, because it made them think of the elderly lady and her husband. They said they would come back to the bakery next Saturday and say hello to her again.

Tim and Liz are twins. They like to play in the garden with their toys. One day, they find a big box of prunes on the table. Prunes are sweet and chewy. Tim and Liz want to eat them all.

But Mom says, "No, you can't eat them all. They are for Grandma. She is coming to visit us. You can have one each, but no more."

Tim and Liz are sad. They love Grandma, but they love prunes too. They sneak back to the table when Mom is not looking. They take two prunes each and hide them in their pockets.

Then they go to the swing. They swing high and low. They laugh and sing. They forget about the prunes in their pockets.

But the prunes are not happy. They are hot and squishy. They start to leak juice. The juice stains Tim and Liz's clothes. It makes them sticky and smelly.

Mom sees them and says, "What have you done? You are so foolish! You ruined your clothes and wasted the prunes. Grandma will be here soon. You have to change and wash up. And no more prunes for you!"

Tim and Liz are sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We were greedy and sneaky. We won't do it again."

Mom hugs them and says, "I forgive you, but you have to learn. Prunes are good, but too many are bad. You have to share and be honest. And you have to stretch before you swing. It's good for your muscles."

Tim and Liz nod and say, "Yes, Mom. We will stretch and share and be honest. And we will say sorry to Grandma too."

They go to their room and change. They wash their faces and hands. They stretch their arms and legs. They feel better. They are ready to see Grandma and give her a hug. And maybe one prune each.

Tim and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Tim had a toy snake that he liked to wrap around his arm and scare Lily. Lily had a toy mouse that she liked to hide under the sofa and make squeak.

"Look, Lily, I have a big snake!" Tim said, holding his toy snake in front of Lily's face. "It can bite you and make you sick!"

Lily was not afraid of Tim's snake. She knew it was harmless and made of plastic. She smiled and said, "No, Tim, your snake is not big. It is very small. See, it is only an inch long!" She took a ruler and measured Tim's snake. "My mouse is bigger than your snake!"

Tim was not happy that Lily said his snake was small. He wanted to have the biggest and scariest toy. He said, "No, Lily, your mouse is not bigger. It is very tiny. See, it can fit in my hand!" He grabbed Lily's mouse and held it up. "My snake can eat your mouse!"

Lily was not happy that Tim took her mouse. She wanted to have her toy back. She said, "No, Tim, give me my mouse! It is mine and I love it!" She reached for her mouse and tried to pull it from Tim's hand.

Tim and Lily started to tug and pull on the mouse. They both wanted to have it and did not want to share. They did not notice that their mom was watching them from the kitchen. She saw them fighting and decided to teach them a lesson.

She came into the living room and said, "Tim, Lily, what are you doing? Why are you fighting over a toy? Don't you know that toys are for playing, not for hurting?" She took the mouse and the snake from their hands and said, "If you can't play nicely with your toys, then you can't have them at all. I will wrap them up and put them away until you learn to share and be kind."

Tim and Lily were sad and sorry. They did not want to lose their toys. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We were silly and mean. Please, can we have our toys back? We will share and be nice."

Mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you are sorry. But you have to show me that you mean it. How about you wrap up one of your toys and give it to the other as a present? Then you can say thank you and play together."

Tim and Lily thought that was a good idea. They said, "OK, Mom, we will do that." They took some paper and tape and wrapped up their toys. Then they gave them to each other and said, "Here, this is for you. I'm sorry for being mean. Thank you for being my friend."

Mom was proud of Tim and Lily. She said, "That's very nice of you. I'm happy that you are friends. Now you can play with your toys and have fun. But remember, be gentle and careful with them. They are harmless, but they are not real. They are only toys."

Sara and Ben love spring. Spring is when the sun is warm and the flowers grow. Spring is when they can play outside and see the birds and the bugs. Sara and Ben like to make things with the things they find in spring. They make crowns with leaves and flowers. They make boats with sticks and leaves. They make houses with rocks and mud.

One day, Sara and Ben find something unusual in spring. They find a big egg in a nest. The egg is not like the eggs they see in the farm. The egg is blue and shiny and has spots. Sara and Ben wonder what is inside the egg. They want to make a new friend.

They take the egg to their house. They put the egg in a basket with grass and flowers. They give the egg some water and some bread. They sing to the egg and tell it stories. They wait for the egg to hatch.

The next day, Sara and Ben hear a noise from the basket. They run to see the egg. The egg is cracking. Something is coming out of the egg. Sara and Ben are excited and scared. They see a head, then a body, then a tail. The thing that comes out of the egg is not a bird or a bug. It is a dragon.

The dragon is small and cute. It has scales and wings and horns. It has blue eyes and a pink tongue. It looks at Sara and Ben and makes a sound. It sounds like "mama" and "papa". Sara and Ben smile. They hug the dragon and give it a name. They name it Sparky. They make a new friend in spring.

Sara loves tuna. She eats tuna every day for lunch. She likes to open the can and put the tuna on bread. She does not like to share her tuna with anyone.

One day, Sara finds a huge can of tuna in the pantry. She is very happy. She thinks it is her lucky day. She takes the can and runs to the kitchen. She does not mind that the can is heavy. She wants to eat all the tuna by herself.

She looks for the can opener. She cannot find it. She asks her mom. Her mom says the can opener is broken. She says she will buy a new one later. She tells Sara to eat something else for lunch.

Sara is very sad. She does not want to eat something else. She wants to eat the huge can of tuna. She puts the can on the table and cries. She does not see the cat.

The cat sees the can of tuna. The cat loves tuna too. The cat jumps on the table and sniffs the can. The cat sees a small hole in the can. The cat licks the hole. The cat tastes the tuna. The cat is very happy.

The cat bites the hole. The hole gets bigger. The cat bites the hole again. The hole gets even bigger. The cat bites the hole one more time. The can pops open. The tuna spills out. The cat eats the tuna. The cat does not mind that the tuna is messy. The cat wants to eat all the tuna by itself.

Sara hears a noise. She stops crying. She looks at the table. She sees the cat. She sees the can. She sees the tuna. She screams. She is very angry. She does not like to share her tuna with anyone. She runs to the table and tries to grab the can. The cat hisses and scratches her. The cat does not like to share its tuna with anyone.

Sara and the cat fight over the tuna. They make a lot of noise. They make a big mess. They do not see mom.

Mom hears the noise. She stops working. She goes to the kitchen. She sees Sara and the cat. She sees the can. She sees the tuna. She gasps. She is very shocked. She does not like to see her tuna wasted. She says the tuna was for dinner. She says the can was huge. She says it was enough for everyone. She says Sara and the cat should have minded their manners. She scolds Sara and the cat. She makes them clean up the mess. She makes them eat something else for lunch. She does not give them any tuna.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a small bird in a tree. The bird has a red head and a yellow body. It makes a pretty sound.

"Wow, look at that bird!" Sara says. "What is its name?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "But I want to catch it. It is so pretty."

Ben gets a net and tries to catch the bird. But the bird is fast and smart. It flies away from the net. Ben runs after the bird. He does not see the big rock in his way. He trips and falls. He hurts his knee. He cries.

Sara runs to help Ben. She sees his knee is bleeding. She gets a band-aid from her bag and puts it on his knee. She hugs him and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?"

Ben stops crying. He says, "Thank you, Sara. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I tried to catch the bird. It was not nice. The bird is free and happy. It does not want to be in a net."

Sara smiles and says, "That's okay, Ben. I'm glad you learned your lesson. The bird is happy to make its sound in the tree. We can listen to it and enjoy it. We don't need to catch it."

They sit on the grass and listen to the bird. They are happy too.

The end.

"No, it is mine. I saw it first," Lila says. She holds the bear tight.

"But we found it together. It is not fair," Tom says. He tries to grab the bear.

"Stop it! Go away!" Lila says. She pushes Tom away.

Tom falls down and hurts his knee. He cries. Lila does not care. She shrugs and looks at the bear.

"Ha, ha, I have the bear. You have nothing," she says.

She does not see the big hole in the box. She does not see the snake that comes out of the hole. It is green and has black spots. It is angry. It bites Lila on the arm.

Lila screams. She drops the bear. She feels pain. She cries.

Tom sees the snake. He is scared. He runs away. He does not help Lila.

Lila is alone. She is hurt. She is sad.

Lily was confused. "How does it help us find our way home?" she asked.

"Well," her mom explained, "when we get lost, we can look for the North Star and it will guide us back home."

Lily was amazed. She looked up at the star and said, "Wow! The North Star is so special!" Suddenly, the wind started to blow and it got very cold. "Mommy, I'm freezing," Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. Let's go inside and warm up," her mom said. And they went inside to drink hot cocoa and snuggle up together.

After playing with the bunny for a while, Lily went back inside to take a bath. She used her favorite green bath toy and washed herself with soap and shampoo. As she was getting ready for bed, Lily thought about the bunny and hoped it was feeling better. She fell asleep dreaming of playing with the bunny again tomorrow. The end.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the kitchen. She saw her mom making cookies on a tray. Mia wanted to help her mom, so she asked, "Mom, can I help you?" Her mom said, "Yes, Mia, you can help me. But be careful, the tray is hot."

Mia helped her mom put the cookies on the tray. When the cookies were ready, her mom let Mia hold the tray. But Mia forgot that the tray was hot. She touched it and said, "Ouch! It is hot!" Her mom told her, "I told you to be careful, Mia. The tray is hot."

Mia felt sad that she didn't listen to her mom. She said, "I am sorry, Mom. I will listen to you next time." Her mom hugged her and said, "It is okay, Mia. Just remember to listen and be careful."

The moral value of the story is to always listen to the people who care for you, as they want to keep you safe.

Next, it was Bird's turn. "Tweet!" Cat, Dog, and Fish guessed it was a bird sound. Finally, it was Fish's turn. Fish made a sound, but it was very quiet. The friends had to listen very carefully. They heard a soft "bloop" sound. Cat, Dog, and Bird guessed it was a fish sound, and they were right! The team was successful in guessing all the sounds because they worked together and listened to each other. The friends learned that working together as a team can help them do great things.

"No, no, no!" Mia says, holding her doll tightly. "This is not a castle, this is my house! And this is not a princess, this is my doll! Go away, Tim!"

Rip!

The doll's head comes off. Mia gasps. Tim gasps. They both look at the doll's head in Tim's hand and the doll's body in Mia's hand. They both start to cry.

"Mama, mama, mama!" Mia wails, running to the kitchen. "Tim broke my doll! He broke my doll!"

Mama comes out of the kitchen. She sees the doll's head and the doll's body. She sees Mia and Tim crying. She is very angry.

"What did you do?" Mama asks, frowning. "Why did you break Mia's doll? That was very naughty, Tim!"

He wants to say sorry to Mia. But Mama does not let him. She takes his fire truck away. She takes him to his room. She closes the door.

Tim is alone in his room. He is sad. He is sorry. He is bored. He wishes he had not broken Mia's doll. He wishes he had not insisted that there was a fire. He wishes he had listened to Mia. He wishes he had been a better brother. He wishes he had a better ending.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a farm. They liked to play with the animals, but they did not like to help with the chores. One day, their father asked them to feed the goat. Ben and Sam did not want to do it. They said, "The goat is not fun. The goat is not cute. The goat is not useful. Why do we have to feed the goat?"

Their father was angry. He said, "The goat is very useful. The goat gives us milk and cheese. The goat eats the grass and weeds. The goat keeps us company. You should be kind to the goat and feed him every day. If you do not feed the goat, you will not get any milk or cheese or grass or company."

Ben and Sam did not listen. They ran away to play with the dog and the cat. They forgot about the goat. The goat was hungry and lonely. He started to yell. He yelled very loud. He yelled, "Baa! Baa! Baa!"

The father heard the goat. He went to see what was wrong. He saw that the goat had no food or water. He was very sad. He said, "Poor goat. You are so useful, but no one cares for you. I will feed you and give you water. I will pet you and talk to you. You are a good goat."

The goat was happy. He stopped yelling. He said, "Maa! Maa! Maa!" He licked the father's hand. He thanked him for his kindness.

Ben and Sam heard the goat and the father. They felt ashamed. They realized that they were wrong. They said, "We are sorry, father. We are sorry, goat. We were selfish and rude. We did not appreciate you. You are very useful and very nice. Can we help you feed the goat and give him water? Can we pet him and talk to him? Can we be his friends?"

The father smiled. He said, "Yes, you can. I am glad that you learned your lesson. The goat is a part of our family. We should treat him with respect and love. He will reward us with his gifts and his friendship. Come, let us feed the goat together."

Ben and Sam nodded. They followed their father. They fed the goat and gave him water. They petted him and talked to him. They became his friends. The goat was happy. He said, "Baa! Baa! Baa!" He gave them milk and cheese and grass and company. They all lived happily on the farm.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to animals. They are useful and friendly. They deserve our care and attention. They will make us happy and grateful.

As he was looking at the animals, Timmy heard a loud noise. He quickly became alert and looked around to see what was happening. It was just the elephants trumpeting. Timmy was relieved and continued to enjoy his day at the zoo.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went for a walk. They saw a garden with pretty flowers. Lily wanted to enter the garden to smell the flowers. 

But her mom said, "No, Lily. The gate is closed." 

Lily looked sad. Suddenly, a pale man appeared. He said, "Hello, little girl. Do you want to enter the garden?" 

Lily nodded her head. The man smiled and opened the gate. Lily and her mom entered the garden. They smelled the flowers and felt happy. "Thank you," said Lily. "You're welcome," said the pale man. And then he disappeared.

Later that day, Ellie and her friends decided to have a parade. They all marched around the jungle, singing and dancing. Ellie was the leader of the parade and everyone followed her. The mouse was so happy to be a part of the parade, she marched under Ellie's big, kind feet.

From that day on, Ellie and the mouse became the best of friends. They shared peanuts and had many more parades together. Ellie was happy to have such a wonderful friend under her big, kind heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a furry teddy bear that she loved very much. One night, Lily went to bed and had a dream about her teddy bear. In her dream, her teddy bear could talk!

"Hello Lily!" said the teddy bear. "I'm so happy to see you!"

Lily was so excited to hear her teddy bear talk. "Wow! You can talk!" she exclaimed.

Suddenly, the teddy bear started to fall off the bed. "Oh no!" cried Lily. "Be careful, teddy bear!"

But the teddy bear just laughed and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'm a tough bear. I can handle a little fall." And with that, he landed safely on the floor.

Lily was so happy to have her furry teddy bear back in her arms. "I'm so glad you're okay," she said. "I love you, teddy bear."

"I love you too, Lily," said the teddy bear. And with that, Lily fell back asleep, dreaming of all the adventures she and her teddy bear would have together.

Red was so happy that he zoomed all around town, showing off his shiny motor. And from that day on, Red always made sure to take good care of his motor so it would never sound troubled again.

From that day on, Lily and her brother shared the couch and watched TV together. They learned that sharing and being kind to each other was the best way to solve conflicts.

Max's owner was happy to see the ball and threw it for Max to chase. Max ran after the ball and jumped into a big puddle, splashing water everywhere. His owner laughed and said, "Max, you sure love to play in the water!"

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie loved to fly high in the sky and soar like an eagle. One day, Tweetie met a wise old owl who asked, "What number do you want to fly to today?" Tweetie didn't understand what the owl meant, so the owl explained, "A number is like a special place you want to go to. It can be high or low, fast or slow."

Tweetie thought for a moment and said, "I want to fly to the number 10!" The owl smiled and said, "Okay, but remember to take it slow and steady." So Tweetie flapped her wings and flew up, up, up towards the number 10. She flew slowly and carefully, enjoying the view along the way.

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew Tweetie off course and she started to fall. "Help!" she cried out. The wise old owl heard her and flew to her side. "Don't worry," he said, "I'll help you soar back up to the number 10." And with a gentle push, Tweetie soared back up to her goal. From that day on, Tweetie learned to fly slow and steady, and she always remembered the wise old owl's advice.

They take turns to push the car and watch it zoom. Sometimes it zooms so fast that it hits the wall or the door. Sometimes it zooms so high that it lands on the bed or the shelf. Lily and Ben laugh and clap their hands.

But their cat, Max, does not like the new car. He is a lazy cat who likes to sleep on the sofa. He does not like the noise and the movement of the car. He thinks it is annoying and scary. He tries to hide under the pillow or behind the curtain.

One time, the car zooms so close to Max that he jumps up and runs away. He knocks over a vase and a lamp. Lily and Ben hear the crash and stop playing. They go to see what happened. They find Max hiding under the bed. They see the broken vase and the lamp.

They feel sorry for Max. They realize they were too loud and too fast. They decide to put away the new car and play with their other toys. They also give Max a hug and a treat. They say sorry to him and to their mom. They learn to be more careful and kind.

Mom says, "You are doing great, Tom. Reading is fun and useful. But you also need to take care of your books. Books are not like rocks or sticks. They can get dirty or torn. You need to keep them clean and safe. Do you know how to do that?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He says, "I can put them in a shelf. I can use a cloth to wipe them. I can be gentle with them. Is that right, Mom?"

Mom says, "That is right, Tom. You are a smart and caring boy. I am proud of you. Now, let's read some more of this book. It is a story about a dog who finds a friend. Do you like dogs, Tom?"

Tom says, "I love dogs, Mom. Maybe I can find a dog someday. And we can read books together." Mom and Tom laugh and hug. They read the book and enjoy their time. Tom is happy with his find.

Lily and Max finished their dinner quickly and asked for their dessert. Mom cut two slices of cake and gave them to the twins. They were very grateful and said thank you. But they also wanted more cake. They looked at the rest of the cake on the table and wondered if they could have another slice.

"I dare you to take another slice," Max whispered to Lily. "Mom won't notice."

Lily looked at Max and then at the cake. She was tempted, but she was also scared. "What if mom sees us?" she whispered back. "She will be angry and we will be in trouble."

Max shrugged. "She won't see us. She is busy in the kitchen. Come on, it's just one more slice. It's so yummy."

Lily hesitated, but then she nodded. She reached for the cake and took another slice. She gave half of it to Max and they ate it quickly. They smiled at each other and licked their fingers.

But then they heard mom's voice. "Lily, Max, what are you doing?" Mom came into the room and saw the cake. She saw the missing slice and the crumbs on the twins' faces. She was not happy. Lily and Max felt bad. They knew they had done something wrong. They said sorry to mom and went to their room. They wished they had not taken the extra slice. Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy boat. They took it to the pond and put it in the water. They watched it float and move with the wind.

"Let's rock the boat!" Ben said. He threw a stone at the boat and made a big splash. The boat rocked and tipped over.

"Stop it, Ben! That's not nice!" Sam said. He ran to the edge of the pond and tried to reach the boat. But it was too far and he slipped and fell into the water.

"Help! Help!" Sam cried. He was scared and wet. The water was cold and deep.

Ben felt sorry for his brother. He ran to get help. He saw a man with a big, powerful dog. The dog had a red collar and a shiny badge.

"Please, sir, please help my brother! He fell into the pond!" Ben said.

The man and the dog ran to the pond. The dog jumped into the water and swam to Sam. He grabbed Sam's shirt with his teeth and pulled him to the shore. The man helped Sam out of the water and wrapped him in a blanket.

"Are you okay, son?" the man asked.

"Yes, thank you, sir. And thank you, doggy. You are very brave and powerful," Sam said.

The man smiled and petted the dog. "His name is Rex. He is a rescue dog. He helps people who are in trouble."

Ben hugged his brother and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong to rock the boat. I won't do it again. I love you."

Sam hugged him back and said, "I love you too, Ben. And I love Rex. He is our hero."

The moral of the story is: Don't rock the boat. It can cause trouble and danger. Be kind and respectful to others. And be grateful to those who help you.

"Mom, can I catch the frog?" he asked.

"Be careful, Tom. Frogs are slippery and they can jump very high. You might scare it away," his mom said.

Tom did not listen. He ran to the rock and reached for the frog. But the frog was faster. It jumped into the water and vanished.

"Where did it go?" Tom cried. He looked around, but he could not see the frog.

"It's gone, Tom. It hid under the water. Maybe it will come back later, if you are quiet and patient," his mom said.

Tom was sad and angry. He wanted the frog. He did not want to wait. He stomped his feet and threw a stick into the pond.

"Stop that, Tom. You are making too much noise. You are scaring the other animals. That's not nice," his mom said.

Tom did not care. He wanted the frog. He did not want to be nice. He threw another stick into the pond.

But then, something happened. The water splashed and a big green head popped out. It was the frog. It looked at Tom with its big eyes and opened its mouth.

"Ribbit! Ribbit!" it said.

Tom was surprised. He stopped throwing sticks. He looked at the frog.

"Did you say something?" he asked.

"Ribbit! Ribbit!" the frog said again.

Tom did not understand. He did not speak frog. He wondered what the frog was saying.

"Are you trying to talk to me?" he asked.

"Ribbit! Ribbit!" the frog said louder.

Tom was curious. He wanted to know what the frog was saying. He forgot about catching it and playing with it. He wanted to listen to it and learn from it.

He sat down on the grass and smiled at the frog.

"Hello, frog. I'm sorry I scared you. I want to be your friend. Can you teach me how to speak frog?" he asked.

The frog smiled back. It nodded its head and said:

"Ribbit! Ribbit!"

Anna was sad and angry. She saw a shiny purse on a shelf. It was enormous and had many colors. Anna thought, "I want that purse. It is so pretty. Mom will not see me." She took the purse and hid it under her coat.

Mom paid for the things and said, "Come on, Anna, let's go home." Anna followed mom, but she felt guilty. She knew she did a bad thing. She wanted to tell mom, but she was afraid.

On the way home, a lady stopped them. She said, "Excuse me, miss, I think your daughter has my purse. I left it on the shelf by mistake. It is very important to me. It has my keys, my phone, and my medicine."

Mom was shocked. She looked at Anna and saw the bulge under her coat. She said, "Anna, is that true? Did you take the lady's purse?" Anna nodded and started to cry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, lady. I wanted the purse. It was so pretty. But I know it was wrong. Please forgive me."

The lady was kind and said, "Thank you for being honest, Anna. I forgive you. But you must learn to respect other people's things. And you must listen to your mom. She knows what is best for you." She took the purse and gave Anna a hug.

Mom was sad and said, "Anna, I'm disappointed in you. You should not steal. It is a very bad thing. You could have hurt the lady and yourself. You must always stay with me and do what I say. I love you and I want you to be good and happy." She hugged Anna and said, "I forgive you, too. But you must promise me to never do that again."

Anna said, "I promise, mom. I love you, too. And I'm sorry. I don't need the purse. I have you and that is enough." They went home and mom gave Anna a kiss and a cookie.

The end.

Moral: Stealing is wrong and hurts others and yourself. You should be grateful for what you have and listen to your parents. They love you and want the best for you.

Ben looked at the lamp and the bird and the ball. He felt sorry. He wagged his tail and licked Sam's face.

"I'm sorry, Sam. I did not mean to sneeze. It was the flower. It made me sneeze."

Sam smiled and hugged Ben. He was not angry. He knew Ben was a good dog.

"It's okay, Ben. It was an accident. You are still my famous dog. And I still love you."

Ben was happy. He loved Sam too. He barked and ran to get the ball. He hoped he would not sneeze again.

One day, Daddy went outside to pick some flowers. He put on his jacket and asked his little girl if she wanted to come with him. She was so excited!

But when Daddy and little girl arrived at the garden they saw a sad sight. Someone had picked all of the flowers in the garden. Daddy was so sorry. He felt bad for the garden and put his arm around his little girl.

Just then, Daddy had an idea. He asked his little girl to pick the sunset. Together they ran to the beach and watched the sun set over the ocean. His little girl was so excited and loved the sight.

The next day, Daddy went back to the garden to explain why he and his little girl had picked the sunset. He was so sorry and brought some new flowers for the garden. The gardener was happy to see the beautiful new flowers and thanked Daddy for understanding. Daddy and his little girl smiled and went back home.

Michael was an unfriendly boy. He always refused to talk to his classmates. His teacher tried to be nice to him, but he never answered her questions.

One day, the teacher asked Michael to take the sack with bones to the other side of the school. But Michael refused to do it. He yelled at the teacher, "No!"

The teacher got angry. She called Michael a deaf boy and told him to take the sack with bones right away.

Michael was frightened and he didn't want to make the teacher angry, so he went to take the sack with bones. He was going to carry it across the school field.

Suddenly, a big wind came and brought some strong storms. It swept the sack away and Michael couldn't catch it. Without the sack, Michael was very sad and lonely. He had to go home with his head low and empty-handed.

Once upon a time, there was a lion who lived in a big, messy forest. The lion was very strong and brave, and loved to roar. Every day, he roamed around the forest and enjoyed the sound of his loud roar.

One day, the lion was walking near a small stream. He saw a tasty, juicy fish swimming in the water, and he decided to take a closer look.

The lion said to the fish, "I am going to catch you!" The fish swam quickly away, but the lion was fast. He lunged out of the stream and grabbed the fish in his mouth.

But the stream was strong and wild, and the lion was pulled down into the water. He tried to get back up, but the water was too powerful. The lion roared one last time and disappeared into the messy depths.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Thomas. He was only three years old and he loved playing outdoors.

One day, he came across a silver box. It was really shiny, so he got really excited. He tried to open it, but it was too tight.

He called out to his mum, "Mum! I found a silver box!"

His mum smiled and said, "Oh, that's great! But make sure you don't care it too much. You might hurt yourself."

Thomas was careful, but he was still really curious. Eventually, he managed to open the box and when he did, out came lots and lots of bees. They started to buzz around Thomas and he was so scared that he started to cry.

His mum rushed over to help and try to shoo the bees away, but the bees kept coming back. Eventually, Thomas had lots of sting marks all over his body. 

His mum was really sad that he'd been stung, but she was still glad that Thomas had been careful.

Once upon a time, there was a deep lake. Near the lake there lived a family. The family was very poor and they had almost no money. One day, the father said to the mother, "We must try to get some money. We will close our eyes and jump into the lake." 

The mother was worried and said, "But the lake is very deep. What if something bad happens?" 

The father said, "It is a risk we must take. We will close our eyes and hope for the best!"

So the father and mother closed their eyes, crossed their fingers and jumped! They were waiting for a few moments and suddenly they heard a loud splashing noise. They opened their eyes and saw a big bag of money floating in the middle of the lake!

The father smiled and said, "Look, I told you that when we close our eyes and take a chance, good things will happen!"

The family was very happy, and from that day, they always remembered that when taking a risk, the reward can be deep.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lila. She loved playing outside, running around and singing her favorite songs. One day, it started to get dark and so Lila's mom called her inside.

Once she was inside, Lila's mom said, "Lila, let's play a game. I'm going to hide your phone and you have to find it!" Lila was excited to start the game so she quickly ran around the house trying to find the phone.

Suddenly, Lila heard a loud noise outside the window. She ran to the window to see what it was. When she looked out, she saw a big, scary monster! She quickly ran back to her mom, screaming.

"Mom, there's a scary monster outside! What should I do?" She asked in a frightened voice. Her mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lila. I'm here. Let's just keep playing our game and ignore the monster."

So Lila and her mom continued their game. Eventually, Lila was able to find her phone and the scary monster vanished. At the end of the game, Lila was so proud of herself for finding her phone, even with a scary monster outside!

Sammy was in the park, swinging on the swings. He was going so high that he felt he could touch the clouds. All of a sudden, he saw an ostrich on the far side of the playground. He had never seen an ostrich before, so he was very excited. 

He shouted out to the ostrich and it came closer. Sammy said hello, but the ostrich only stared back. Sammy smiled, but the ostrich didn't pay much attention. 

Sammy began to feel frustrated. He asked the ostrich if he could join him on the swings and the ostrich said nothing. Sammy gave up and went back to the swings. He kept swinging and soon enough, the ostrich started to swing too!

Sammy smiled as he watched the ostrich swing. He was having so much fun. He realised that the ostrich had been trying to join him all along.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who did not like desserts. She was very fearful of trying any new food and this made her parents very sad.

One day, her parents took her to the store and pointed at a big chocolate cake in the window. The little girl shook her head and said: "No, I don't want it". Her parents tried to persuade her to try it, but she still refused.

She went home feeling scared and upset. She thought that she was never going to be able to try new things and felt sad all day.

The next day, her parents asked her to try a different dessert and the little girl felt scared. She shook her head and said "No, I'm still scared". Her parents were very disappointed, but there was nothing they could do.

The little girl never tried any desserts again and she never got to overcome her fear.
